title.zh: 卷七十五 列傳第六十五 隱逸上
title.raw: 卷七十五 列傳第六十五 隱逸上 Volume 75 Biographies 65: Recluses 1

sentences.zh: 陶潛 宗少文 沈道虔 孔淳之 周續之 戴顒 翟法賜 雷次宗 郭希林 劉凝之 龔祈 朱百年 關康之 漁父 褚伯玉 顧歡 杜京產

translations.literal: Tao Qian, Zong Shaowen, Shen Daoqian, Kong Chunzhi, Zhou Xuizhi, Dai Yong, Zhai Fasi, Lei Cizong, Guo Xilin, Liu Ningzhi, Gong Qi, Zhu Bainian, Guan Kangzhi, the Fisherman, Chu Boyu, Gu Huan, Du Jingchan
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian; Zong Shaowen; Shen Daoqian; Kong Chunzhi; Zhou Xuizhi; Dai Yong; Zhai Fasi; Lei Cizong; Guo Xilin; Liu Ningzhi; Gong Qi; Zhu Bainian; Guan Kangzhi; the Fisherman; Chu Boyu; Gu Huan; and Du Jingchan

sentences.zh: 陶潛，字淵明，或云字深明，名元亮。

translations.literal: Tao Qian, styled Yuanming; some say his style was Shenming; his name was Yuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian, whose style was Yuanming—though some say Shenming—was named Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 尋陽柴桑人，晉大司馬侃之曾孫也。

translations.literal: A man of Chaisang in Xunyang; he was the great-grandson of Jin Grand Marshal Tao Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He was from Chaisang in Xunyang, great-grandson of the Jin Grand Marshal Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 少有高趣，宅邊有五柳樹，故常著五柳先生傳云：

translations.literal: In youth he had lofty inclinations; five willow trees stood beside his dwelling, so he often composed the Biography of Master Five Willows, which says:
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held lofty tastes; five willows grew beside his home, and he often wrote the Biography of Master Five Willows, which runs:

sentences.zh: 先生不知何許人，不詳姓字。

translations.literal: The Master does not know from what place he comes; his surname and personal name are not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Master’s birthplace is unknown; neither surname nor given name is recorded.

sentences.zh: 閒靜少言，不慕榮利。

translations.literal: Quiet and sparing of speech, he does not covet glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring and sparing of speech, he cared nothing for rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，不求甚解，每有會意，欣然忘食。

translations.literal: He loves reading books and does not seek thorough understanding; whenever he grasps the meaning, he forgets eating in delight.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books without insisting on exhaustive mastery; whenever meaning dawned on him, he would forget his meal in joy.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，而家貧不能恒得。

translations.literal: By nature he is fond of wine, yet the family is poor and cannot constantly obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was in his nature, but poverty kept the house from a steady supply.

sentences.zh: 親舊知其如此，或置酒招之，造飲輒盡，期在必醉。

translations.literal: Kin and friends, knowing this of him, sometimes set out wine to summon him; arriving to drink he would drain it all, his aim being sure drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends, knowing his ways, would sometimes lay out wine and invite him; he would drink it dry at once, resolved always to end drunk.

sentences.zh: 既醉而退，曾不吝情去留。

translations.literal: When drunk he withdraws, never stinting feeling over going or staying.
translations.idiomatic: Once drunk he would take his leave, never troubling himself over comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 環堵蕭然，不蔽風日，裋褐穿結，簞瓢屢空，晏如也。

translations.literal: The bare rooms are desolate, not sheltering from wind and sun; coarse cloth is patched and torn, the basket and gourd often empty—yet he is at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His bare rooms stood empty, open to wind and sun; his hemp coat was patched and threadbare, his basket and gourd often empty—yet he remained serene.

sentences.zh: 常著文章自娛，頗示己志，忘懷得失，以此自終。

translations.literal: He often composes writings to amuse himself, showing rather his intent; forgetting gain and loss, he ends his days thus.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote often for his own pleasure, revealing his mind; forgetting profit and loss, he lived out his days in that spirit.

sentences.zh: 其自序如此。

translations.literal: His self-account is as above.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his self-portrait.

sentences.zh: 蓋以自況，時人謂之實錄。

translations.literal: It was essentially to mirror himself; men of the time called it a true record.
translations.idiomatic: It was essentially self-portraiture; contemporaries called it an honest account.

sentences.zh: 親老家貧，起為州祭酒，不堪吏職，少日自解而歸。

translations.literal: His parents were aged and the family poor; he took office as libationer of the province, could not bear official duties, and after a few days resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: With aged parents and a poor household, he accepted the post of provincial libationer; unable to endure official service, he resigned after a few days and went home.

sentences.zh: 州召主簿，不就，躬耕自資，遂抱羸疾。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk; he did not go, plowed for his own support, and then fell into chronic wasting illness.
translations.idiomatic: The province summoned him as chief clerk, but he refused; he tilled the fields to support himself and eventually fell into chronic wasting illness.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史檀道濟往候之，偃臥瘠餒有日矣，道濟謂曰：「夫賢者處世，天下無道則隱，有道則至。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jiangzhou, Tan Daoji, went to visit him; he had lain ill and famished for days. Daoji said to him, "When the worthy dwell in the world, if the realm is without the Way they hide; if there is the Way they emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji, Inspector of Jiangzhou, came to call on him. Qian had lain ill and starving for days. Daoji said, "When the worthy live in the world, in times without the Way they withdraw; when the Way prevails they come forth.

sentences.zh: 今子生文明之世，奈何自苦如此。」

translations.literal: Now you are born in an age of culture and brightness—why torment yourself thus?
translations.idiomatic: You are born in an age of culture and light—why afflict yourself like this?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「潛也何敢望賢，志不及也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "How would Qian dare aspire to worthiness? My aim does not reach that far.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "How would I dare claim to be worthy? My resolve does not rise to that."

sentences.zh: 道濟饋以粱肉，麾而去之。

translations.literal: Daoji presented him with grain and meat; he waved him away and sent it off.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji offered him grain and meat; he waved him off and had the gift taken away.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮軍、建威參軍，謂親朋曰：「聊欲弦歌，以為三徑之資，可乎？」

translations.literal: Later he served as aide to the Pacifying Army and the Establishing Might Army; he told kin and friends, "I merely wish to pluck the lute and sing—to earn the upkeep of three paths, would that do?
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as aide to the Pacifying and Establishing Might armies. He told kin and friends, "I only mean to pluck the lute and sing—to earn upkeep for three garden paths. Would that suffice?

sentences.zh: 執事者聞之，以為彭澤令。

translations.literal: Those in charge heard this and made him magistrate of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge heard of it and appointed him magistrate of Pengze.

sentences.zh: 不以家累自隨，送一力給其子，書曰：「汝旦夕之費，自給為難，今遣此力，助汝薪水之勞。

translations.literal: He did not bring his household with him; he sent one laborer to his son, writing, "Your morning and evening expenses are hard to supply on your own; now I send this man to help with your chores of firewood and water.
translations.idiomatic: He did not bring his family along; he sent one laborer to his son with a letter: "Your daily needs are hard to meet alone; I send this man to help with firewood and water.

sentences.zh: 此亦人子也，可善遇之。」

translations.literal: He too is another man’s son; you should treat him kindly.
translations.idiomatic: He is someone else’s son as well; treat him kindly.

sentences.zh: 公田悉令吏種秫稻，妻子固請種粳，乃使二頃五十畝種秫，五十畝種粳。

translations.literal: All the official fields he ordered the clerks to plant glutinous rice; his wife firmly asked to plant non-glutinous rice, so he had two hundred fifty mu plant glutinous and fifty mu plant non-glutinous.
translations.idiomatic: He had all official fields planted with glutinous rice; his wife insisted on common rice, so he allotted two hundred fifty mu to glutinous and fifty to common.

sentences.zh: 郡遣督郵至縣，吏白應束帶見之。

translations.literal: The commandery sent an inspecting clerk to the county; the clerk reported that he should gird himself and go to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery sent an inspecting clerk to the county; a clerk said he ought to gird himself and go to receive him.

sentences.zh: 潛歎曰：「我不能為五斗米折腰向鄉里小人。」

translations.literal: Qian sighed and said, "I cannot bow my waist for five pecks of rice before village petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Qian sighed and said, "I cannot bend my waist for five pecks of rice before village petty men.

sentences.zh: 即日解印綬去職，賦歸去來以遂其志，曰：

translations.literal: That same day he surrendered seal and sash and left office; he composed Returning Home to fulfill his intent, saying:
translations.idiomatic: That very day he surrendered seal and sash and left office; he wrote Returning Home to fulfill his resolve, saying:

sentences.zh: 歸去來兮，田園將蕪胡不歸？

translations.literal: Home I go—how can I not return, when fields and garden lie waste?
translations.idiomatic: Home I go—how can I not return, when fields and garden lie waste?

sentences.zh: 既自以心為形役兮，奚惆悵而獨悲。

translations.literal: Since I have let the heart be slave to the form, why brood and grieve alone?
translations.idiomatic: Having let the heart be slave to the body, why brood and grieve alone?

sentences.zh: 悟已往之不諫，知來者之可追。

translations.literal: I realize the past cannot be admonished; I know what is to come can be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: I see the past cannot be warned back; I know what lies ahead may yet be sought.

sentences.zh: 實迷塗其未遠，覺今是而昨非。

translations.literal: Truly I had strayed but the wrong road was not far; now I know today is right and yesterday wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I had strayed, but the wrong road was not far; now I know today is right and yesterday wrong.

sentences.zh: 舟遙遙以輕揚，風飄飄而吹衣，問征夫以前路，恨晨光之熹微。

translations.literal: The boat drifts far, lightly rising; the wind flutters and blows my robe; I ask the boatman the road ahead and regret the dawn light is dim.
translations.idiomatic: The boat drifts lightly onward; wind flutters my robe; I ask the boatman the road ahead and regret how dim the dawn still is.

sentences.zh: 乃瞻衡宇，載欣載奔，僮僕歡迎，弱子候門。

translations.literal: Then I gaze at my house across the beam; now joy, now running; servants welcome me; my little son waits at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: I gaze at my house across the threshold—now glad, now running; servants welcome me; my little son waits at the gate.

sentences.zh: 三徑就荒，松菊猶存，攜幼入室，有酒盈樽。

translations.literal: The three paths are nearly overgrown, yet pines and chrysanthemums remain; I lead the young indoors—wine fills the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The three paths are nearly overgrown, yet pines and chrysanthemums remain; I lead the young indoors—wine fills the cup.

sentences.zh: 引壺觴而自酌，眄庭柯以怡顏，倚南窗而寄傲，審容膝之易安。

translations.literal: I draw the jug and pour for myself; I glance at courtyard branches to ease my face; I lean on the south window in proud ease and see how easily contentment fills a knee’s breadth of room.
translations.idiomatic: I draw the cup and pour for myself; I glance at courtyard boughs to ease my face; I lean on the south window in proud ease and find how easily a knee’s breadth of room brings peace.

sentences.zh: 園日涉而成趣，門雖設而常關。

translations.literal: Daily I tread the garden and it becomes delight; the gate is set yet often shut.
translations.idiomatic: Each day I walk the garden and pleasure grows; the gate stands but stays often closed.

sentences.zh: 策扶老以流憩，時矯首而遐觀。

translations.literal: I lean on my staff and rest where the stream wanders; sometimes I lift my head and gaze into the distance.
translations.idiomatic: I lean on my staff where the stream wanders; sometimes I lift my head and gaze afar.

sentences.zh: 雲無心以出岫，鳥倦飛而知還。

translations.literal: Clouds without heart issue from the crag; birds weary of flight know to return.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds without intent drift from the ridge; birds weary of flight know to return.

sentences.zh: 景翳翳其將入，撫孤松而盤桓。

translations.literal: The light dims and will enter; I stroke the lone pine and linger.
translations.idiomatic: Light dims toward evening; I stroke the lone pine and linger.

sentences.zh: 歸去來兮，請息交以絕遊，世與我而相遺，復駕言兮焉求。

translations.literal: Home I go—let me cease companionship and cut off wandering; the world and I leave each other; why drive my words and seek again?
translations.idiomatic: Home I go—let me end companionship and cut off travel; the world and I have parted; why drive my words and seek again?

sentences.zh: 悅親戚之情話，樂琴書以消憂，農人告餘以春及，將有事於西疇。

translations.literal: I delight in intimate talk with kin; I rejoice in zither and books to dispel sorrow; farmers tell me spring has come and work awaits in the western field.
translations.idiomatic: I delight in kin’s intimate talk; I rejoice in zither and books to ease sorrow; farmers tell me spring has come and work awaits in the western field.

sentences.zh: 或命巾車，或棹扁舟，既窈窕以窮壑，亦崎嶇而經丘。

translations.literal: Sometimes I order the cloth-covered cart, sometimes pole a small boat; now through quiet ravines to their end, now over rugged hills along the heights.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes I order the covered cart, sometimes pole a small boat—through quiet ravines to their end, over rugged hills along the heights.

sentences.zh: 木欣欣以向榮，泉涓涓而始流，善萬物之得時，感吾生之行休。

translations.literal: Trees flourish and turn toward glory; springs trickle and begin to flow; I approve how the ten thousand things gain their season and feel my own life’s course nearing its close.
translations.idiomatic: Trees flourish toward spring; springs trickle and begin to flow; I rejoice that the ten thousand things gain their season and feel my own life’s course nearing its close.

sentences.zh: 已矣乎，寓形宇內復幾時，曷不委心任去留，胡為遑遑欲何之。

translations.literal: It is done—how long may form lodge within the universe? Why not entrust the heart and leave going or staying? Why hurry and haste—whither would you go?
translations.idiomatic: It is done—how long may form lodge within the universe? Why not entrust the heart and leave going or staying? Why hurry and haste—whither would you go?

sentences.zh: 富貴非吾願，帝鄉不可期。

translations.literal: Wealth and honor are not my wish; the Emperor’s domain cannot be awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and honor are not my wish; the Emperor’s domain cannot be awaited.

sentences.zh: 懷良辰以孤往，或植杖而芸耔。

translations.literal: I cherish fine days and go alone, or plant my staff and weed the seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: I cherish fine days and go alone, or plant my staff and weed the seedlings.

sentences.zh: 登東皋以舒嘯，臨清流而賦詩，聊乘化以歸盡，樂夫天命復奚疑。

translations.literal: I climb the eastern height and give a long whistle; by the clear stream I compose verse; for a while I ride transformation to the end and rejoice in Heaven’s mandate—what doubt remains?
translations.idiomatic: I climb the eastern height and give a long whistle; by the clear stream I compose verse; for a while I ride transformation to the end and rejoice in Heaven’s mandate—what doubt remains?

sentences.zh: 義熙末，徵為著作佐郎，不就。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yixi era he was summoned as Assistant Editor; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yixi era he was summoned as Assistant Editor but declined.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史王弘欲識之，不能致也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, Inspector of Jiangzhou, wished to know him but could not bring him in.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, Inspector of Jiangzhou, wished to know him but could not secure a meeting.

sentences.zh: 潛嘗往廬山，弘令潛故人龐通之齎酒具于半道栗裏要之。

translations.literal: Qian once went to Mount Lu; Hong had his old friend Pang Tongzhi carry wine and vessels halfway to Chestnut Lane to waylay him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian once went to Mount Lu; Hong had his old friend Pang Tongzhi carry wine and vessels halfway to Chestnut Lane to waylay him.

sentences.zh: 潛有腳疾，使一門生二兒舉籃轝。

translations.literal: Qian had an ailment of the foot and had a student and two sons lift a basket sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had a foot ailment and had a student and two sons carry him in a basket litter.

sentences.zh: 及至，欣然便共飲酌，俄頃弘至，亦無忤也。

translations.literal: When he arrived they drank together in delight; presently Hong came, yet there was no offense.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived they drank together gladly; soon Hong came as well, and Qian showed no displeasure.

sentences.zh: 先是，顏延之為劉柳後軍功曹，在尋陽與潛情款。

translations.literal: Before this, Yan Yanzhi had been merit officer to Liu Liu’s Rear Army; in Xunyang he was on intimate terms with Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan Yanzhi had served as merit officer to Liu Liu’s Rear Army; in Xunyang he was on intimate terms with Qian.

sentences.zh: 後為始安郡，經過潛，每往必酣飲致醉。

translations.literal: Later, as magistrate of Shi’an Commandery, passing Qian’s place, each visit ended in deep drinking until drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Shi’an, whenever he passed Qian’s home their meetings ended in deep drinking until drunk.

sentences.zh: 弘欲要延之一坐，彌日不得。

translations.literal: Hong wished to have Yanzhi sit together with him; for a whole day he could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong wished to have Yanzhi sit with Qian for a day, but could not arrange it.

sentences.zh: 延之臨去，留二萬錢與潛，潛悉送酒家稍就取酒。

translations.literal: As Yanzhi was leaving he left twenty thousand cash with Qian; Qian sent it all to the wine shop to draw wine as needed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi was leaving he left twenty thousand cash with Qian, who sent it all to the wine shop to draw wine as needed.

sentences.zh: 嘗九月九日無酒，出宅邊菊叢中坐久之。

translations.literal: Once on the ninth day of the ninth month he had no wine; he went out and sat long beside the chrysanthemums by his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the Double Ninth he had no wine; he went out and sat long among the chrysanthemums beside his house.

sentences.zh: 逢弘送酒至，即便就酌，醉而後歸。

translations.literal: He met Hong sending wine; he drank at once, got drunk, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hong arrived with wine; he drank at once, grew drunk, and went home.

sentences.zh: 潛不解音聲，而畜素琴一張。

translations.literal: Qian did not understand music, yet he kept one plain zither.
translations.idiomatic: Qian did not understand music, yet he kept one plain zither.

sentences.zh: 每有酒適，輒撫弄以寄其意。

translations.literal: Whenever wine was at hand he would stroke and play it to lodge his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever wine was at hand he would stroke it to lodge his intent.

sentences.zh: 貴賤造之者，有酒輒設。

translations.literal: Whether noble or base, whoever came to him—if there was wine he would set it out.
translations.idiomatic: Noble or humble, whoever came—if there was wine he would set it out.

sentences.zh: 潛若先醉，便語客：「我醉欲眠卿可去。」

translations.literal: If Qian grew drunk first he would tell the guest, "I am drunk and wish to sleep—you may go.
translations.idiomatic: If he grew drunk first he would tell guests, "I am drunk and wish to sleep—you may go.

sentences.zh: 其真率如此。

translations.literal: His genuine forthrightness was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his genuine forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 郡將候潛，逢其酒熟，取頭上葛巾漉酒，畢，還復著之。

translations.literal: The commandery general waited on Qian; finding his wine ready, he took the hemp turban from his head to strain the wine, then put it on again when done.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery general called on Qian; finding his wine ready, Qian took the hemp turban from his head to strain it, then put it on again when done.

sentences.zh: 潛弱年薄宦，不潔去就之跡。

translations.literal: In his weak years Qian held minor office; his record of going and staying was not spotless.
translations.idiomatic: In his younger years Qian held minor office; his record of accepting and refusing posts was not spotless.

sentences.zh: 自以曾祖晉世宰輔，恥復屈身後代，自宋武帝王業漸隆，不復肯仕。

translations.literal: He considered that his great-grandfather had been a Jin-era chief minister and felt shame at bowing again to a later dynasty; from the time Emperor Wu of Song’s royal enterprise rose steadily, he would no longer serve.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather had been a Jin chief minister; he was ashamed to bow to a later house, and once Emperor Wu of Song’s enterprise rose steadily he would serve no more.

sentences.zh: 所著文章，皆題其年月。

translations.literal: In all writings he composed he inscribed the year and month.
translations.idiomatic: In every work he wrote he dated the year and month.

sentences.zh: 義熙以前，明書晉氏年號，自永初以來，唯雲甲子而已。

translations.literal: Before the Yixi era he clearly wrote the Jin dynastic reign; from the Yongchu era onward he wrote only the sexagenary cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yixi he wrote the Jin reign titles clearly; from Yongchu onward he noted only the sexagenary year.

sentences.zh: 與子書以言其志，並為訓戒曰：

translations.literal: In a letter to his sons he stated his intent and also set down admonitions, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In a letter to his sons he stated his intent and left admonitions, saying:

sentences.zh: 吾年過五十，而窮苦荼毒。

translations.literal: I have passed fifty and suffer bitter poverty.
translations.idiomatic: I have passed fifty and live in bitter poverty.

sentences.zh: 性剛才拙，與物多忤。

translations.literal: By nature I am stiff and blunt in talent and at odds with much in the world.
translations.idiomatic: By nature I am stiff and blunt, at odds with much in the world.

sentences.zh: 自量為己，必貽俗患。

translations.literal: Measuring for myself, I am sure to bring worldly trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Judging myself, I am sure to bring worldly trouble.

sentences.zh: 僶俛辭事，使汝幼而饑寒耳。

translations.literal: Stooping to leave office has made you, while young, know hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: My stooping to leave office has left you hungry and cold while still young.

sentences.zh: 常感孺仲賢妻之言，敗絮自擁，何慚兒子。

translations.literal: I often feel the words of Ru Zhong’s worthy wife—wrapping herself in worn cotton, what shame before her sons?
translations.idiomatic: I often recall the worthy wife of Ru Zhong—wrapping herself in rags, what shame before her sons?

sentences.zh: 此既一事矣。

translations.literal: This is already one matter.
translations.idiomatic: That is one matter settled.

sentences.zh: 但恨鄰靡二仲，室無萊婦，抱茲苦心，良獨罔罔。

translations.literal: I only regret having no Zhong of the neighborhood, no Lai woman in the house—bearing this bitter heart, I am quite alone and lost.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret having no Zhong for a neighbor, no Lai woman at home—bearing this bitter heart, I stand quite alone.

sentences.zh: 少來好書，偶愛閑靖，開卷有得，便欣然忘食。

translations.literal: From youth I have loved books and casually loved quiet ease; opening a book with gain, I forget eating in delight.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I have loved books and quiet ease; when a book rewards me I forget my meal in delight.

sentences.zh: 見樹木交蔭，時鳥變聲，亦復歡爾有喜。

translations.literal: Seeing trees cast overlapping shade and season birds change their calls, I am again glad and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When trees cast overlapping shade and season birds change their calls, I am glad again.

sentences.zh: 嘗言五六月北窗下臥，遇涼風暫至，自謂是羲皇上人。

translations.literal: He once said that lying north of the window in the fifth or sixth month, when a cool breeze came for a moment, he called himself a man of the time of Emperor Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that lying north of the window in the fifth or sixth month, when a cool breeze came, he felt himself a man of Emperor Xi’s age.

sentences.zh: 意淺識陋，日月遂往，疾患以來，漸就衰損。

translations.literal: My intent is shallow and my understanding crude; days and months pass; since illness came I have gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: My mind is shallow and my learning crude; days pass; since illness came I have gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 親舊不遺，每有藥石見救，自恐大分將有限也。

translations.literal: Kin and friends do not abandon me; whenever they offer medicine and stone to save me, I fear my allotted span is nearly spent.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends do not abandon me; whenever they offer remedies I fear my allotted span is nearly spent.

sentences.zh: 汝輩幼小，家貧無役，柴水之勞，何時可免。

translations.literal: You are still young; the family is poor and without servants; the labor of firewood and water—when can it end?
translations.idiomatic: You are still young; the house is poor and without servants—when will the labor of firewood and water end?

sentences.zh: 念之在心，若何可言。

translations.literal: Keeping it in the heart—how can it be spoken?
translations.idiomatic: It weighs on my heart beyond words.

sentences.zh: 然雖不同生，當思四海皆兄弟之義。

translations.literal: Yet though not born of the same mother, you should think on the meaning that within the four seas all are brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Though not born of one mother, remember that within the four seas all men are brothers.

sentences.zh: 鮑叔、敬仲，分財無猜，歸生、伍舉，班荊道舊，遂能以敗為成，因喪立功。

translations.literal: Bao Shu and Jing Zhong divided wealth without suspicion; Gui Sheng and Wu Ju broke branches to speak of old days—thus they could turn defeat into success and achieve merit through loss.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Shu and Jing Zhong shared wealth without suspicion; Gui Sheng and Wu Ju broke branches to recall old days—thus they turned defeat to success and made merit from loss.

sentences.zh: 佗人尚爾，況共父之人哉。

translations.literal: If others are thus, how much more those who share one father?
translations.idiomatic: If strangers can be thus, how much more those who share one father?

sentences.zh: 潁川韓元長，漢末名士，身處卿佐，八十而終，兄弟同居，至於沒齒。

translations.literal: Han Yuanchang of Yingchuan was a famed man of late Han; though he held ministerial rank he lived to eighty; brothers dwelt together until the end of their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuanchang of Yingchuan was a late Han man of renown; though he reached ministerial rank he lived to eighty, and brothers dwelt together to the end of their days.

sentences.zh: 濟北泛幼春，晉時操行人也。

translations.literal: Fan Youchun of Jibei was a man of upright conduct in Jin times.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Youchun of Jibei was a man of upright conduct in Jin times.

sentences.zh: 七世同財，家人無怨色。

translations.literal: Seven generations shared one purse; the household showed no color of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations shared one purse; no one in the household showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「高山景行」，汝其慎哉。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "Lofty mountain, broad path"—take care, you two.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Lofty mountain, broad path"—take care, my sons.

sentences.zh: 又為命子詩以貽之。

translations.literal: He also composed the Poem to Command the Son and bequeathed it to them.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Poem to Command the Son and left it to them.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，將復徵命，會卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia he was about to be summoned again when he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia a summons was about to go out when he died.

sentences.zh: 世號靖節先生。

translations.literal: The world styles him Master Tranquil Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The world styles him Master Tranquil Integrity.

sentences.zh: 其妻翟氏，志趣亦同，能安苦節，夫耕于前，妻鋤于後云。

translations.literal: His wife was the Zhai clan; her aims were likewise the same; she could abide bitter integrity—he plowed in front, she hoed behind, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was of the Zhai clan, of like mind, able to abide bitter integrity—he plowed ahead, she hoed behind, it is said.

sentences.zh: 宗少文

translations.literal: Zong Shaowen
translations.idiomatic: Zong Shaowen

sentences.zh: 宗少文，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Zong Shaowen was a man of Nieyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Shaowen was from Nieyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖承，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng was Governor of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 父繇之，湘鄉令。

translations.literal: His father Yaozhi was magistrate of Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yaozhi was magistrate of Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 母同郡師氏，聰辯有學義，教授諸子。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Shi clan of the same commandery—clever, eloquent, learned in righteousness, and she instructed her sons.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was of the Shi clan of the same commandery—clever, eloquent, learned in righteousness—and she instructed her sons.

sentences.zh: 少文善居喪，為鄉閭所稱。

translations.literal: Shaowen was skilled in dwelling in mourning and was praised by village and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowen was skilled in mourning rites and praised throughout his district.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝既誅劉毅，領荊州，問毅府諮議參軍申永曰：「今日何施而可？」

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Song had executed Liu Yi and taken charge of Jingzhou, he asked Yi’s former staff adviser Shen Yong, "What measures should be taken today?
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Song executed Liu Yi and took Jingzhou, he asked Yi’s former adviser Shen Yong, "What should be done today?

sentences.zh: 永曰：「除其宿釁，倍其惠澤，貫敘門次，顯擢才能，如此而已。」

translations.literal: Yong said, "Remove old grievances, double gracious favors, set forth kin in order of seniority, and clearly promote talent—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Remove old grievances, double gracious favors, set kin in order of seniority, and clearly promote talent—that is all."

sentences.zh: 武帝納之，乃辟少文為主簿，不起，問其故。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted this and summoned Shaowen as chief clerk; he did not rise and was asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted this and summoned Shaowen as chief clerk; he declined and was asked why.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「棲丘飲穀，三十餘年。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Dwelling on the hill and drinking valley grain for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have dwelt on the hill and drunk valley grain for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 武帝善其對而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his reply and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved his reply and desisted.

sentences.zh: 少文妙善琴書圖畫，精於言理，每遊山水，往輒忘歸。

translations.literal: Shaowen was masterly at zither, books, and painting, and skilled in discourse on principle; whenever he roamed mountains and rivers he would forget to return.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowen excelled at zither, books, and painting and was skilled in discourse on principle; roaming mountains and rivers he often forgot to return.

sentences.zh: 征西長史王敬弘每從之，未嘗不彌日也。

translations.literal: Wang Jinghong, chief clerk to the Pacifying West, often followed him; never was a day not spent in full.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinghong, chief clerk to the Pacifying West, often accompanied him; their outings never lasted less than a full day.

sentences.zh: 乃下入廬山，就釋慧遠考尋文義。

translations.literal: He then went down into Mount Lu and with the monk Huiyuan examined and sought the meaning of texts.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Mount Lu and with the monk Huiyuan pursued textual meaning.

sentences.zh: 兄臧為南平太守，逼與俱還，乃於江陵三湖立宅，閒居無事。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zang was Governor of Nanping and forced him to return together; he then built a dwelling at the Three Lakes of Jiangling and lived in retirement without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zang, Governor of Nanping, forced him to return; he built a dwelling at Jiangling’s Three Lakes and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 武帝召為太尉行參軍，驃騎道憐命為記室參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him as acting aide to the Grand Marshal; the Rapid Cavalry General Dao Lian appointed him record keeper—he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him as acting aide to the Grand Marshal; General Dao Lian of the Rapid Cavalry appointed him record keeper—he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 二兄早卒，孤累甚多，家貧無以相贍，頗營稼穡。

translations.literal: Two elder brothers died early; he had many orphaned dependents; the family was poor and could not support them, so he rather cultivated crops.
translations.idiomatic: Two elder brothers died young; many dependents fell to him; the house was too poor to support them, so he took rather to farming.

sentences.zh: 人有餉遺，並受之。

translations.literal: When people sent gifts he accepted them all.
translations.idiomatic: When people sent gifts he accepted them all.

sentences.zh: 武帝敕南郡長給吏役，又數致餼賚。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the magistrate of Nan Commandery to supply clerks and laborers and repeatedly sent provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the magistrate of Nan Commandery to supply clerks and laborers and repeatedly sent provisions.

sentences.zh: 後子弟從祿，乃悉不復受。

translations.literal: Later, when younger kinsmen took salaries, he would accept no more.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when younger kinsmen took salaries, he accepted no more.

sentences.zh: 武帝開府辟召，下書召少文與雁門周續之並為太尉掾，皆不起。

translations.literal: When the Emperor opened his headquarters and issued summons, he sent documents summoning Shaowen and Zhou Xuizhi of Yanmen as aides to the Grand Marshal; neither rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor opened his headquarters he summoned Shaowen and Zhou Xuizhi of Yanmen as aides to the Grand Marshal; neither accepted.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪及元嘉中頻征，並不應。

translations.literal: When Song received the mandate and through the Yuanjia era he was repeatedly summoned, he never responded.
translations.idiomatic: When Song received the mandate and through the Yuanjia era he was repeatedly summoned, he never responded.

sentences.zh: 妻羅氏亦有高情，與少文協趣。

translations.literal: His wife, the Luo clan, also had lofty feeling and shared Shaowen’s bent.
translations.idiomatic: His wife of the Luo clan also had lofty feeling and shared his bent.

sentences.zh: 羅氏沒，少文哀之過甚，既乃悲情頓釋，謂沙門釋慧堅曰：「死生之分，未易可達，三復至教，方能遣哀。」

translations.literal: When Lady Luo died Shaowen grieved beyond measure; then his passionate sorrow suddenly released itself; he told the monk Huijian, "The boundary between life and death is not easily reached; only after thrice reviewing the highest teaching could I send grief away.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Luo died he grieved beyond measure; then passion suddenly released itself. He told the monk Huijian, "The boundary of life and death is hard to reach; only after thrice reviewing the highest teaching could I send grief away.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季為荊州，親至其室，與之歡宴，命為諮議參軍，不起。

translations.literal: Prince Yiji of Hengyang was in Jingzhou; he came in person to his room and feasted with him, appointing him staff adviser—he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiji of Hengyang, in Jingzhou, came in person to feast with him and appointed him staff adviser—he declined.

sentences.zh: 好山水，愛遠遊，西陟荊、巫，南登衡嶽，因結宇衡山，欲懷尚平之志。

translations.literal: He loved mountains and waters and distant travel; west he climbed Jing and Wu, south he ascended Mount Heng; he built a house on Mount Heng wishing to cherish the resolve of Shang Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He loved mountains, waters, and distant travel—west to Jing and Wu, south to Mount Heng; he built on Mount Heng, wishing to cherish Shang Ping’s resolve.

sentences.zh: 有疾還江陵，歎曰：「老疾俱至，名山恐難遍睹，唯澄懷觀道，臥以遊之。」

translations.literal: Illness brought him back to Jiangling; he sighed, "Old age and illness have both arrived; famous mountains I fear I cannot see in full—only by clearing the heart and observing the Way, lying down to roam them.
translations.idiomatic: Illness brought him back to Jiangling; he sighed, "Old age and illness have both come; I fear I cannot see all the famous peaks—only by clearing the heart and observing the Way, roaming them while lying down.

sentences.zh: 凡所遊履，皆圖之於室，謂之「撫琴動操，欲令眾山皆響」。

translations.literal: Every place he traveled he painted in his room, saying he wished "to stroke the zither and move the air, making all mountains sound."
translations.idiomatic: Every place he traveled he painted in his room, saying he wished "to stroke the zither and move the air until every mountain resounded."

sentences.zh: 古有金石弄，為諸桓所重，桓氏亡，其聲遂絕，唯少文傳焉。

translations.literal: Of old there was the metal-and-stone piece cherished by the Huan clan; when the Huans perished its sound ceased—only Shaowen transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Of old there was a metal-and-stone piece the Huan clan cherished; when the Huans perished its sound died—only Shaowen kept it alive.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣樂師楊觀就受之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent the music master Yang Guan to receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent the music master Yang Guan to learn it from him.

sentences.zh: 少文孫測，亦有祖風。

translations.literal: Shaowen’s grandson Ce also had his grandfather’s manner.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowen’s grandson Ce also had his grandfather’s manner.

sentences.zh: 測字敬微，一字茂深，家居江陵。

translations.literal: Ce, styled Jingwei, also styled Maoshen, dwelt at home in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Ce, styled Jingwei and also Maoshen, lived at home in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 少靜退，不樂人間。

translations.literal: From youth he was quiet and retiring, not delighting in the world of men.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quiet and retiring, taking no delight in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「家貧親老，不擇官而仕，先哲以為美談，餘竊有惑。

translations.literal: He sighed, "The family is poor and parents aged—choosing office without discrimination the ancients called fine talk; I myself am doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "The house is poor and parents aged—choosing any office without scruple the ancients praised; I myself am doubtful.

sentences.zh: 誠不能潛感地金，冥致江鯉，但當用天之道，分地之利。

translations.literal: Truly I cannot secretly move earth-gold or darkly bring river carp, but one should use Heaven’s way and share the earth’s profit.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot secretly move earth to gold or darkly summon river carp, but one should use Heaven’s way and share the earth’s profit.

sentences.zh: 孰能食人厚祿，憂人重事乎？」

translations.literal: Who can eat others’ thick salary yet bear others’ heavy affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Who can eat thick salary yet bear others’ heavy burdens?"

sentences.zh: 齊驃騎豫章王嶷徵為參軍，不起，測答府云：「何為謬傷海鳥，橫斤山木。」

translations.literal: Prince Yi of the Rapid Cavalry, King of Yuzhang, summoned him as aide; he did not rise. Ce replied to the headquarters, "Why wrongly wound the sea bird and swing the axe at mountain trees?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of the Rapid Cavalry, King of Yuzhang, summoned him as aide; he declined. Ce replied to the headquarters, "Why wrongly wound the sea bird and swing an axe at mountain trees?

sentences.zh: 母喪，身自負土，植松柏。

translations.literal: At his mother’s mourning he himself carried earth and planted pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother’s mourning he carried earth himself and planted pines and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 嶷復遣書請之，辟為參軍。

translations.literal: Yi again sent a letter inviting him and appointed him aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yi again sent a letter inviting him and appointed him aide.

sentences.zh: 測答曰：「性同鱗羽，愛止山壑，眷戀松雲，輕迷人路。

translations.literal: Ce answered, "By nature I am like scales and feathers; my love stops at mountain valleys; I cherish pine clouds and lightly esteem the road of men.
translations.idiomatic: Ce answered, "By nature I am like fish and bird; my love stops at mountain valleys; I cherish pine clouds and lightly esteem the road of men.

sentences.zh: 縱宕岩流，有若狂者，忽不知老至。

translations.literal: Wandering recklessly along cliffs and streams, there are times like madness when suddenly I do not know old age has come.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering recklessly along cliffs and streams, there are times like madness when suddenly I do not know old age has come.

sentences.zh: 而今鬢已白，豈容課虛責有，限魚鳥慕哉。」

translations.literal: But now my temples are white—how can I accept empty duty and debt, limited like fish and birds in longing?"
translations.idiomatic: But now my temples are white—how can I accept empty duty and debt, limited like fish and birds in longing?"

sentences.zh: 永明三年，詔征太子舍人，不就。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he was ordered summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming he was summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent but did not go.

sentences.zh: 欲游名山，乃寫祖少文所作尚子平圖於壁上。

translations.literal: Wishing to roam famous mountains, he painted on the wall his ancestor Shaowen’s picture of Master Shang Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to roam famous mountains, he painted on the wall his ancestor Shaowen’s picture of Master Shang Ping.

sentences.zh: 測長子賓宦在都，知父此旨，便求祿還為南郡丞，測遂付以家事。

translations.literal: Ce’s eldest son Bin held office in the capital; knowing his father’s intent, he sought a salary and returned as aide to the Governor of Nan Commandery; Ce then entrusted household affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ce’s eldest son Bin held office in the capital; knowing his father’s intent, he sought a post and returned as aide to the Governor of Nan Commandery; Ce then entrusted the household to him.

sentences.zh: 刺史安陸王子敬、長史劉寅以下皆贈送之，測無所受，齎老子，莊子二書自隨。

translations.literal: The Inspector Anlu Prince Zijing, Chief Clerk Liu Yin, and those below all sent farewell gifts; Ce accepted none, taking only the Laozi and Zhuangzi as companions.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Prince Zijing of Anlu, Chief Clerk Liu Yin, and others sent farewell gifts; Ce accepted none, taking only the Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 子孫拜辭悲泣，測長嘯不視，遂往廬山，止祖少文舊宅。

translations.literal: Descendants bowed farewell in grief and weeping; Ce gave a long whistle without looking and went to Mount Lu, stopping at his ancestor Shaowen’s old dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants bowed farewell in tears; Ce gave a long whistle without looking and went to Mount Lu, lodging at his ancestor Shaowen’s old house.

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響為江州，厚遣贈遺。

translations.literal: Marquis Zixiang of Yufu was in Jiangzhou and sent rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zixiang of Yufu, in Jiangzhou, sent rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 測曰：「少有狂疾，尋山采藥，遠來至此，量腹而進松術，度形而衣薜蘿，淡然已足，豈容當此橫施。」

translations.literal: Ce said, "From youth I have had wild illness; I seek mountains to gather medicine and have come far to this place—measuring my belly I take pine fare, fitting my form I wear vine robes; plain ease is already enough—how can I accept such lavish bestowal?
translations.idiomatic: Ce said, "From youth I have had wild illness; I seek mountains for medicine and have come far—measuring my belly I take pine fare, fitting my form I wear vine robes; plain ease is enough—how can I accept such lavish gifts?

sentences.zh: 子響命駕造之，測不見。

translations.literal: Zixiang ordered his carriage to visit him; Ce did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang ordered his carriage to visit; Ce did not appear.

sentences.zh: 後子響不告而來，奄至所住，測不得已，巾褐對之，竟不交言。

translations.literal: Later Zixiang came without announcing himself and suddenly reached his lodging; Ce had no choice but to meet him in headcloth and coarse robe, yet in the end exchanged no words.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zixiang came unannounced and suddenly reached his lodging; Ce met him in headcloth and coarse robe but exchanged no words.

sentences.zh: 子響不悅而退。

translations.literal: Zixiang was displeased and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang was displeased and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 侍中王秀之彌所欽慕，乃令陸探微畫其形與己相對，又貽書曰：「昔人有圖畫僑、劄，輕以自方耳。」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Wang Xiuzhi greatly admired him and had Lu Tanwei paint his likeness facing his own; he also sent a letter saying, "Men of old painted Qiao and Zha and lightly set themselves beside them.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wang Xiuzhi greatly admired him and had Lu Tanwei paint his likeness facing his own; he wrote, "Men of old painted Qiao and Zha and lightly set themselves beside them.

sentences.zh: 王儉亦雅重之，贈以蒲褥筍席。

translations.literal: Wang Jian also esteemed him highly and gave him rush mats and bamboo mats.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian also esteemed him highly and gave him rush and bamboo mats.

sentences.zh: 頃之，測送弟喪還西，仍留舊宅永業寺，絕賓友，唯與同志庾易、劉虯、宗人尚之等往來講說。

translations.literal: Before long Ce escorted his younger brother’s coffin west and remained at the old dwelling, Yongye Temple, cutting off guests; only with like-minded men Yu Yi, Liu Qiu, and his clansman Shangzhi did he come and go in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ce escorted his younger brother’s coffin west and stayed at the old Yongye Temple dwelling, cutting off guests; only with Yu Yi, Liu Qiu, and his clansman Shangzhi did he discourse.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史隨王子隆至鎮，遣別駕宗忻口致勞問。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou, Prince Zilong of Sui, on reaching his post sent his vice-governor Zong Xin orally to convey courteous inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zilong of Sui, Inspector of Jingzhou, on reaching his post sent Vice-Governor Zong Xin to convey courteous inquiry.

sentences.zh: 測笑曰：「貴賤理隔，何以及此。」

translations.literal: Ce laughed and said, "Noble and base are separated by principle—how does it reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Ce laughed and said, "Noble and base are separated by principle—how does it reach this?

sentences.zh: 竟不答。

translations.literal: In the end he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not answer.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，徵為司徒主簿，不就，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was summoned as chief clerk to the Minister of Education; he did not go and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he was summoned as chief clerk to the Minister of Education; he declined and died.

sentences.zh: 測善畫，自圖阮籍遇蘇門於行鄣上，坐臥對之。

translations.literal: Ce was skilled at painting; he himself painted Ruan Ji meeting Su Men on the road screen and sat facing it whether sitting or lying.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was skilled at painting; he painted Ruan Ji meeting Su Men on a screen and sat or lay facing it.

sentences.zh: 又畫永業佛影台，皆為妙作。

translations.literal: He also painted the Buddha-shadow terrace of Yongye—both were masterworks.
translations.idiomatic: He also painted Yongye’s Buddha-shadow terrace—both were masterworks.

sentences.zh: 好音律，善易、老，續皇甫謐高士傳三卷。

translations.literal: He loved music and was good at the Changes and Laozi; he continued Huangfu Mi’s Biographies of High Men in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music and was skilled in the Changes and Laozi; he continued Huangfu Mi’s Biographies of High Men in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊衡山七嶺，著衡山、廬山記。

translations.literal: He once roamed the seven ridges of Mount Heng and composed records of Mount Heng and Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He once roamed Mount Heng’s seven ridges and wrote records of Mount Heng and Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 尚之字敬文，亦好山澤，徵辟一無所就，以壽終。

translations.literal: Shangzhi, styled Jingwen, also loved mountains and marshes; summons and appointments he accepted none of, and he ended by longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi, styled Jingwen, also loved mountains and marshes; he accepted no summons and died of old age.

sentences.zh: 彧之字叔粲，少文從父弟也。

translations.literal: Youzhi, styled Shucan, was Shaowen’s younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, styled Shucan, was Shaowen’s younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 早孤，事兄恭謹。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he served his elder brother with respectful care.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he served his elder brother with respectful care.

sentences.zh: 家貧好學，雖文義不逮少文，而真澹過之。

translations.literal: The family was poor yet he loved learning; though his literary meaning did not reach Shaowen’s, in genuine plainness he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Poor yet studious, though his literary reach did not match Shaowen’s, in genuine plainness he surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 徵辟一無所就。

translations.literal: Summons and appointments he accepted none of.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no summons or appointment.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉初，大使陸子真觀采風俗，三詣彧之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia the envoy Lu Zizhen came to observe local customs and thrice called on Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanjia the envoy Lu Zizhen came to observe local customs and thrice called on Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 每辭疾不見，告人曰：「我布衣草萊之人，少長壟畝，何宜枉軒冕之客。」

translations.literal: Each time he pleaded illness and would not be seen, telling others, "I am a man in cloth and straw, long grown in the fields—why should I trouble carriage and cap with a visit?
translations.idiomatic: Each time he pleaded illness and would not be seen, telling others, "I am cloth and straw, long grown in the fields—why trouble carriage and cap with a visit?

sentences.zh: 子真還，表薦之，又不就征。

translations.literal: Zizhen returned and memorialized recommending him; again he did not accept summons.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen returned and memorialized recommending him; again he did not accept summons.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 沈道虔

translations.literal: Shen Daoqian
translations.idiomatic: Shen Daoqian

sentences.zh: 沈道虔，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Daoqian was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Daoqian was from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 少仁愛，好老、易，居縣北石山下。

translations.literal: From youth he was benevolent and loving; he loved the Laozi and Changes and dwelt below Stone Mountain north of the county.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was benevolent and loving; he loved the Laozi and Changes and lived below Stone Mountain north of the county.

sentences.zh: 孫恩亂後饑荒，縣令庾肅之迎出縣南廢頭裏，為立宅臨溪，有山水之玩。

translations.literal: After Sun En’s rebellion there was famine; the magistrate Yu Suzhi brought him out to Feitouli south of the county, built a dwelling by the stream with the charm of mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun En’s rebellion came famine; Magistrate Yu Suzhi brought him out to Feitouli south of the county and built a dwelling by the stream amid mountains and waters.

sentences.zh: 時復還石山精廬，與諸孤兄子共釜庾之資，困不改節。

translations.literal: At times he returned to the stone mountain hermitage and with several orphaned elder brothers’ sons shared one pot of grain; though straitened he did not alter his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At times he returned to the stone mountain hermitage and shared one pot of grain with orphaned nephews; though straitened he did not alter his integrity.

sentences.zh: 受琴于戴逵，王敬弘深貴重之。

translations.literal: He received the zither from Dai Kui; Wang Jinghong deeply prized him.
translations.idiomatic: He learned the zither from Dai Kui; Wang Jinghong deeply prized him.

sentences.zh: 郡州府凡十二命，皆不就。

translations.literal: Commandery, province, and headquarters twelve times ordered him—all he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery, province, and headquarters summoned him twelve times; he accepted none.

sentences.zh: 有人竊其園菜者，外還見之，乃自逃隱，待竊者去後乃出。

translations.literal: Someone stole vegetables from his garden; returning from outside he saw it and himself hid away, waiting until the thief left before coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Someone stole vegetables from his garden; returning he saw it and hid himself until the thief left before coming out.

sentences.zh: 人又拔其屋後大筍，令人止之，曰：「惜此筍欲令成林，更有佳者相與。」

translations.literal: Others pulled the large bamboo shoots behind his house; he had people stop them, saying, "I cherish these shoots wishing to make a grove—there are better ones to share with you.
translations.idiomatic: Others pulled large bamboo shoots behind his house; he had people stop them, saying, "I mean these shoots to become a grove—there are better ones to share.

sentences.zh: 乃令人買大筍送與之，盜者慚不取，道虔使置其門內而還。

translations.literal: He then had people buy large bamboo shoots and send them; the thief was ashamed and would not take them—Daoqian had them placed at his gate and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He had large shoots bought and sent; the thief was ashamed and would not take them—Daoqian had them placed at his gate and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 常以捃拾自資，同捃者或爭穟，道虔諫之不止，悉以其所得與之。

translations.literal: He often supported himself by gleaning; among fellow gleaners some quarreled over ears of grain—Daoqian admonished them but they did not stop, so he gave them all he had gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He often lived by gleaning; when fellow gleaners quarreled over ears he admonished them in vain and gave them all he had gathered.

sentences.zh: 爭者愧恧，後每爭輒云：「勿令居士知」。

translations.literal: The quarrelers felt shame; afterward whenever they quarreled they would say, "Do not let the Recluse know.
translations.idiomatic: The quarrelers felt shame; afterward whenever they quarreled they said, "Do not let the Recluse know."

sentences.zh: 冬月無復衣，戴顒聞而迎之，為作衣服，並與錢一萬。

translations.literal: In winter he had no spare clothes; Dai Yong heard and went to welcome him, made clothes for him, and gave ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he had no spare clothes; Dai Yong heard and welcomed him, made clothes, and gave ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 及還，分身上衣及錢悉供諸兄弟子無衣者。

translations.literal: On returning he divided his upper garment and the cash entirely among elder brothers’ sons who had no clothes.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he divided his upper garment and all the cash among nephews who had no clothes.

sentences.zh: 鄉里少年相率受學，道虔常無食以立學徒。

translations.literal: Young men of the village together came to study; Daoqian often had no food yet still maintained students.
translations.idiomatic: Village youths came to study together; Daoqian often had no food yet still kept students.

sentences.zh: 武康令孔欣之厚相資給，受業者咸得有成。

translations.literal: Magistrate Kong Xinzhi of Wukang generously supplied him; those who received instruction all achieved completion.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Kong Xinzhi of Wukang generously supplied him; his students all achieved completion.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝聞之，遣使存問，賜錢三萬，米二百斛，悉供孤兄子嫁娶。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song heard and sent an envoy to inquire after him, bestowing thirty thousand cash and two hundred hu of rice, all supplied for the marriages of orphaned elder brothers’ sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song heard and sent an envoy to inquire, bestowing thirty thousand cash and two hundred hu of rice, all for nephews’ marriages.

sentences.zh: 征員外散騎侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Outer Gentleman Attendant Cavalier; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Outer Gentleman Attendant Cavalier but did not go.

sentences.zh: 累世事佛，推父祖舊宅為寺。

translations.literal: For generations the family served the Buddha; he turned his father and grandfather’s old dwelling into a temple.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family served the Buddha; he turned his forefathers’ old dwelling into a temple.

sentences.zh: 至四月八日每請像，請像之日，輒舉家感慟焉。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month each year he would invite the image; on the day of inviting the image the whole household would be moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the eighth day of the fourth month he would invite the image; on that day the whole household was moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 道虔年老菜食，恒無經日之資，而琴書為樂，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Daoqian in old age ate vegetables; he constantly lacked resources for a full day, yet zither and books were his joy and he never tired.
translations.idiomatic: In old age Daoqian ate vegetables and often lacked a full day’s means, yet zither and books were his joy and he never tired.

sentences.zh: 文帝敕郡縣使隨時資給。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered commandery and county to supply him as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ordered commandery and county to supply him as needed.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子慧鋒，修父業，不就州辟。

translations.literal: His son Huifeng cultivated his father’s pursuit and did not accept provincial summons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huifeng pursued his father’s way and did not accept provincial summons.

sentences.zh: 孔淳之

translations.literal: Kong Chunzhi
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chunzhi

sentences.zh: 孔淳之，字彥深，魯人也。

translations.literal: Kong Chunzhi, styled Yanshen, was a man of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chunzhi, styled Yanshen, was from Lu.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was Gentleman of the Masters of Rites in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan was Gentleman of the Masters of Rites in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父粲，秘書監征，不就。

translations.literal: His father Can was summoned as Secretariat Supervisor; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: His father Can was summoned as Secretariat Supervisor; he did not go.

sentences.zh: 淳之少有高尚，愛好墳籍，為太原王恭所稱。

translations.literal: Chunzhi from youth had lofty character and loved the classics of the tombs; Wang Gong of Taiyuan praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhi from youth had lofty character and loved the classics; Wang Gong of Taiyuan praised him.

sentences.zh: 居會稽剡縣。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Shan County of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Shan County of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 性好山水，每有所遊，必窮其幽峻，或旬日忘歸。

translations.literal: By nature he loved mountains and waters; whenever he traveled he must exhaust their secluded heights, sometimes forgetting to return for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved mountains and waters; on every journey he explored their remotest heights, sometimes forgetting to return for ten days.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊山，遇沙門釋法崇，因留共止，遂停三載。

translations.literal: Once roaming mountains he met the monk Fachong and therefore stayed together; he stopped three years.
translations.idiomatic: Once while roaming the mountains he met the monk Fachong and stayed with him three years.

sentences.zh: 法崇歎曰：「緬想人外三十年矣，今乃傾蓋於茲，不覺老之將至也。」

translations.literal: Fachong sighed and said, "For thirty years I have longed for life beyond men; now at last we meet like overturned carriage covers here—I do not notice old age about to come.
translations.idiomatic: Fachong sighed and said, "For thirty years I have longed for life beyond men; now at last we meet like old friends at a chance encounter—I do not notice old age about to come.

sentences.zh: 及淳之還，乃不告以姓。

translations.literal: When Chunzhi returned, he still did not tell him his surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunzhi returned, he still would not reveal his surname.

sentences.zh: 除著作佐郎、太尉參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Editor and Military Adjutant to the Grand Marshal; he accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Editor and Military Adjutant to the Grand Marshal, but declined both posts.

sentences.zh: 居喪至孝，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: In mourning he was utmost in filial piety, dwelling in a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned with utmost filial devotion, living in a hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 服闋，與征士戴顒、王弘之及王敬弘等共為人外之游，又申以婚姻。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, with the recluses Dai Yong, Wang Hongzhi, and Wang Jinghong he shared travels beyond the world of men, and further extended ties through marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he joined the recluses Dai Yong, Wang Hongzhi, and Wang Jinghong in wanderings apart from worldly affairs, and further bound them through marriage.

sentences.zh: 敬弘以女適淳之子尚，遂以烏羊系所乘車轅，提壺為禮。

translations.literal: Jinghong gave his daughter in marriage to Chunzhi's son Shang; thereupon he tied a black sheep to the shaft of the carriage he rode and, carrying a jug, came with this as his gift.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong gave his daughter to Chunzhi's son Shang in marriage; he then tied a black sheep to his carriage shaft, jug in hand, and came bearing that as his gift.

sentences.zh: 至則盡歡共飲，迄暮而歸。

translations.literal: Upon arrival they drank their fill together in joy and returned only at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived they drank together in full merriment and did not return until evening.

sentences.zh: 或怪其如此，答曰：「固亦農夫田父之禮也。」

translations.literal: Some found this strange; he replied, "After all, this too is the courtesy of farmers and countryfolk."
translations.idiomatic: Some wondered at such conduct; he answered, "This is simply the etiquette of farmers and rustics."

sentences.zh: 會稽太守謝方明苦要之不能致，使謂曰：「苟不入吾郡，何為入吾郭？」

translations.literal: The Governor of Kuaiji, Xie Fangming, pressed him hard but could not bring him in; he sent word: "If you will not enter my commandery, why do you enter my outer city?
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangming, Governor of Kuaiji, importuned him repeatedly but could not win him; he sent a message: "If you refuse to enter my commandery, why do you enter my suburbs?

sentences.zh: 淳之笑曰：「潛遊者不識其水，巢棲者非辯其林，飛沈所至，何問其主。」

translations.literal: Chunzhi smiled and said, "One who roams in hiding does not ask whose waters these are; one who nests in the woods does not dispute whose grove it is — wherever flying or sinking may lead, why ask who is master?
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhi smiled and said, "The hidden wanderer does not inquire whose waters he crosses; the nest-dweller does not argue over whose forest it is — wherever flight or sinking may take one, why ask who is lord?"

sentences.zh: 終不肯往。

translations.literal: In the end he would not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he would not go.

sentences.zh: 茅室蓬戶，庭草蕪徑，唯床上有數帙書。

translations.literal: Thatched hut, brushwood gate, courtyard grass overgrowing the path — upon the bed alone lay a few volumes.
translations.idiomatic: A thatched dwelling with a brushwood door, weeds choking the courtyard path — only a few books upon the bed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，復徵為散騎侍郎，乃逃于上虞縣界，家人莫知所在。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanjia era he was again summoned as Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Library; he fled into the borderlands of Shangyu county, and his household knew not where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanjia he was again summoned as Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Library; he fled into the hills of Shangyu, and his family did not know where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 弟默之為廣州刺史，出都與別，司徒王弘要淳之集冶城，即日命駕東歸，遂不顧也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mozhi was Governor of Guangzhou; on leaving the capital to take leave of him, the Minister over the Masses Wang Hong invited Chunzhi to gather at Yecheng — that same day he ordered his carriage eastward home and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Mozhi was Governor of Guangzhou; as Mozhi left the capital on his way out, Wang Hong, Minister over the Masses, invited Chunzhi to meet at Yecheng — but that very day Chunzhi ordered his carriage homeward to the east and would not attend.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 默之儒學，注谷梁春秋。

translations.literal: Mozhi was a Confucian scholar and annotated the Guliang Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhi was a scholar of the classics and wrote a commentary on the Guliang Annals.

sentences.zh: 默之子熙先，事在范曄傳。

translations.literal: Mozhi's son Xixian — his story is in the biography of Fan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhi's son Xixian is treated in the biography of Fan Ye.

sentences.zh: 周續之

translations.literal: Zhou Xuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuzhi

sentences.zh: 周續之，字道祖，雁門廣武人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuzhi, styled Daozu, was a native of Guangwu in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuzhi, styled Daozu, came from Guangwu in Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 其先過江，居豫章建昌縣。

translations.literal: His forebears had crossed the Yangtze and settled in Jianchang county, Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had crossed south of the river and lived in Jianchang county in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 續之八歲喪母，哀戚過於成人，奉兄如事父。

translations.literal: At eight Xuzhi lost his mother; his grief exceeded that of a grown man, and he served his elder brother as he would a father.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhi lost his mother at eight; his mourning surpassed an adult's, and he served his elder brother as one serves a father.

sentences.zh: 豫章太守范甯于郡立學，招集生徒，遠方至者甚眾。

translations.literal: Fan Ning, Governor of Yuzhang, established a school in the commandery and gathered students; many came from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ning, Governor of Yuzhang, founded a school in the commandery and gathered pupils; students arrived from distant places in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 續之年十二，詣甯受業。

translations.literal: At twelve Xuzhi went to Ning to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, Xuzhi went to study under Ning.

sentences.zh: 居學數年，通五經、五緯，號曰十經，名冠同門，稱為顏子。

translations.literal: After several years at the school he mastered the Five Classics and the Five Wefts, called the Ten Classics; he led his fellow students and was styled "the Yan Hui."
translations.idiomatic: After years of study he mastered the Five Classics and Five Wefts — the so-called Ten Classics — and stood first among his peers, who called him "the Yan Hui."

sentences.zh: 既而閒居讀老、易，入廬山事沙門釋慧遠。

translations.literal: Thereafter he lived in retirement reading the Laozi and the Changes, and entered Mount Lu to serve the monk Shi Huiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew to read the Laozi and the Book of Changes, and went to Mount Lu to study under the monk Huiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時彭城劉遺人遁跡廬山，陶深明亦不應徵命，謂之尋陽三隱。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yiren of Pengcheng had hidden himself on Mount Lu, and Tao Shenming also would not answer summons — they were called the Three Recluses of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yiren of Pengcheng was then in seclusion on Mount Lu, and Tao Shenming likewise refused official appointment; the three were known as the Recluses of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 劉毅鎮姑孰，命為撫軍參軍，征太學博士，並不就。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi held Gucu, he appointed Xuzhi Staff Officer of the Pacification Army and summoned him as Erudite of the Imperial University — he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi governed Gucu he named Xuzhi Pacification Army Staff Officer and summoned him as University Erudite; Xuzhi declined both.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史每相招請，續之不尚峻節，頗從之遊。

translations.literal: The Governors of Jiangzhou often invited him; Xuzhi did not prize lofty austerity and quite often joined their company.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangzhou governors frequently invited him; Xuzhi was not strict about lofty reclusion and often accepted their hospitality.

sentences.zh: 常以嵇康高士傳得出處之美，因為之注。

translations.literal: He always held that Ji Kang's Biographies of Eminent Men showed the beauty of taking office or leaving it, and wrote a commentary on it.
translations.idiomatic: He admired how Ji Kang's Biographies of Eminent Men illuminated the grace of entering and leaving office, and annotated the work.

sentences.zh: 武帝北討，世子居守，迎續之館于安樂寺，延入講禮，月餘復還山。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched north, the heir apparent remained to guard the capital; Xuzhi was received at Anle Monastery to lecture on ritual — after a month and more he returned to the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Emperor's northern campaign the heir apparent stayed behind; Xuzhi was lodged at Anle Monastery to expound ritual, and after more than a month returned to the hills.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史劉柳薦之武帝，俄辟太尉掾，不就。

translations.literal: Liu Liu, Governor of Jiangzhou, recommended him to the Emperor; soon he was summoned as Attendant of the Grand Marshal — he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liu, Governor of Jiangzhou, recommended him to the throne; he was soon invited as Attendant of the Grand Marshal but would not serve.

sentences.zh: 武帝北伐，還鎮彭城，遣使迎之，禮賜甚厚，每曰：「真高士也」。

translations.literal: On the Emperor's northern expedition, returning to garrison Pengcheng, he sent envoys to welcome Xuzhi with generous gifts and courtesies, saying each time, "A true lofty man."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned from the northern campaign to hold Pengcheng, he sent messengers to welcome Xuzhi with rich gifts and honor, repeatedly calling him "a man of true elevation."

sentences.zh: 尋復南還。

translations.literal: Before long he went south again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went south again.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，復召之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne he summoned Xuzhi once more.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took the throne he summoned Xuzhi again.

sentences.zh: 上為開館東郭外，招集生徒，乘輿降幸，並見諸生，問續之禮記「傲不可長」、與我九齡「射於矍圃。」

translations.literal: The sovereign opened a hall east of the outer city wall, gathered students, and descended in his carriage to visit; he saw all the pupils and questioned Xuzhi on the meaning in the Record of Rites of "Arrogance must not grow" and in "Give me your nine years" of "Archery at Juoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor established a school outside the eastern gate, gathered students, and came in person by imperial carriage; he saw the pupils and asked Xuzhi to explain the Record of Rites passage "Arrogance must not be indulged" and the line from "Give me your nine years," "They shot at Juoyuan."

sentences.zh: 之義，辯析精奧，稱為名通。

translations.literal: His analysis was subtle and profound; he was acclaimed as a master of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His exegesis was subtle and profound, and he was hailed as a leading authority.

sentences.zh: 續之素患風痹，不復堪講，乃移病鍾山。

translations.literal: Xuzhi had long suffered from wind paralysis and could no longer bear lecturing; he pleaded illness and moved to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhi had long suffered rheumatism and could lecture no more; citing illness, he retired to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 景平元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Jingping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jingping.

sentences.zh: 通毛詩六義及禮論，注公羊傳，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: He mastered the six meanings of the Mao Odes and treatises on ritual; his commentary on the Gongyang Annals has been handed down.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the six categories of the Mao Odes and in ritual theory; his commentary on the Gongyang Annals survives.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 兄子景遠有續之風。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Jingyuan had Xuzhi's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Jingyuan bore his uncle's character.

sentences.zh: 戴顒字仲若，譙郡銍人也。

translations.literal: Dai Yong, styled Zhongruo, was a native of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yong, styled Zhongruo, was from Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父逵，兄勃，並隱遁有高名。

translations.literal: His father Kui and elder brother Bo both lived in reclusion and had high renown.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui and elder brother Bo were both recluses of high reputation.

sentences.zh: 顒十六遭父憂，幾於毀滅，因此長抱羸患。

translations.literal: At sixteen Yong lost his father; he nearly perished in grief and thereafter remained frail.
translations.idiomatic: Yong lost his father at sixteen and nearly wasted away in mourning; from then on he was chronically weak.

sentences.zh: 以父不仕，復修其業。

translations.literal: Because his father had not served in office, he again cultivated that way of life.
translations.idiomatic: Since his father had never taken office, he too pursued that path.

sentences.zh: 父善琴書，顒並傳之。

translations.literal: His father was skilled at the zither and books; Yong inherited both.
translations.idiomatic: His father excelled at the zither and at calligraphy; Yong mastered both arts.

sentences.zh: 凡諸音律，皆能揮手。

translations.literal: Of all kinds of music he could perform them at a gesture.
translations.idiomatic: He could perform every sort of music at will.

sentences.zh: 會稽剡縣多名山，故世居剡下。

translations.literal: Shan county in Kuaiji had many famous mountains; therefore the family dwelt below Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Shan county in Kuaiji abounded in famous peaks, and the family made their home there.

sentences.zh: 顒及兄勃並受琴于父，父沒，所傳之聲不忍復奏，各造新弄。

translations.literal: Yong and his brother Bo both received the zither from their father; after their father's death they could not bear to play the pieces he had transmitted and each composed new airs.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Bo had learned the zither from their father; after his death they could not bear to play his repertoire and each devised new compositions.

sentences.zh: 勃制五部，顒制十五部，顒又制長弄一部，並傳於世。

translations.literal: Bo composed five suites, Yong fifteen, and Yong also composed one long suite — all handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Bo composed five suites, Yong fifteen, and Yong also one extended suite — all of which circulated.

sentences.zh: 中書令王綏嘗攜客造之，勃等方進豆粥，綏曰：「聞卿善琴，試欲一聽。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat Director Wang Sui once brought guests to visit; Bo and the others were just taking bean porridge. Sui said, "I hear you are skilled at the zither — I should like to hear a piece.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, Secretariat Director, once came with guests; Bo and his brothers were eating bean porridge. Sui said, "I hear you play the zither well — might we hear something?

sentences.zh: 不答，綏恨而去。

translations.literal: They did not answer; Sui left in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: They did not reply; Sui departed in annoyance.

sentences.zh: 桐廬縣又多名山，兄弟復共游之，因留居止。

translations.literal: Tonglu county also had many famous mountains; the brothers again traveled there together and stayed on.
translations.idiomatic: Tonglu too had many celebrated mountains; the brothers traveled there together and settled.

sentences.zh: 勃疾，患醫藥不給。

translations.literal: Bo fell ill; medicine was hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Bo fell ill, and medicine was scarce.

sentences.zh: 顒謂勃曰：「顒隨兄得閒，非有心於語默，兄今疾篤，無可營療，顒當幹祿以自濟耳。」

translations.literal: Yong said to Bo, "I have followed you in leisure — not from any intent to speak or stay silent. Now your illness is grave and there is no way to treat it; I shall seek salary to support us.
translations.idiomatic: Yong told Bo, "I have kept you company in idleness — not from any principle about speech or silence. Your illness is now grave and beyond remedy; I must seek an office to support us.

sentences.zh: 乃求海虞令，事垂行而勃卒，乃止。

translations.literal: He sought the magistracy of Haiyu; the matter was nearly settled when Bo died, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He sought the post of magistrate of Haiyu; the appointment was nearly secured when Bo died, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 桐廬僻遠，難以養疾，乃出居吳下。

translations.literal: Tonglu was remote and hard for tending illness; he went out to live in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Tonglu was too remote for nursing the sick; he moved to the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 吳下土人共為築室，聚石引水，植林開澗，少時繁密，有若自然。

translations.literal: The local people of Wu together built him a house, piled stones to draw water, planted groves and opened streams — in a short time it grew lush, as if by nature.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry of Wu built him a dwelling, laid stone channels for water, planted groves and opened rivulets — soon the place was thick with growth, seemingly untouched by artifice.

sentences.zh: 乃述莊周大旨，著逍遙論、注禮記中庸篇。

translations.literal: He then set forth the great theme of Zhuangzi and wrote the Discourse on Wandering at Ease and a commentary on the Doctrine of the Mean in the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He expounded Zhuangzi's great themes in his Discourse on Wandering at Ease and wrote a commentary on the Doctrine of the Mean.

sentences.zh: 三吳將守及郡內衣冠，要其同遊野澤，堪行便去，不為矯介，眾論以此多之。

translations.literal: The generals and defenders of the Three Wu and the gentry of the commandery, when he wished to roam the marshes and wilds, would go if travel was possible — he made no pretense of stiffness; public opinion therefore praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu commanders and local gentlemen joined his excursions into marsh and wilderness whenever he was fit to travel — he did not affect aloofness, and many esteemed him for it.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建、元嘉中徵，並不就。

translations.literal: When the Song state was first founded and again in the Yuanjia era he was summoned — he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Song and again under Yuanjia he was summoned; he declined each time.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季鎮京口，長史張邵與顒姻通，迎來止黃鵠山，山北有竹林精舍，林澗甚美，顒憩於此澗。

translations.literal: Prince Yiji of Hengyang held Jingkou; the Chief Administrator Zhang Shao, allied to Yong by marriage, welcomed him to Yellow Crane Mountain — north of the mountain was a bamboo hermitage in a fine ravine, and Yong rested in that stream.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiji of Hengyang governed Jingkou; Zhang Shao, Chief Administrator and related by marriage, received Yong at Yellow Crane Mountain, where a bamboo hermitage stood in a lovely glen — Yong made his home by that brook.

sentences.zh: 義季亟從之遊，顒服其野服，不改常度。

translations.literal: Yiji often joined his travels; Yong wore rustic dress and did not change his usual ways.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji often accompanied him on outings; Yong wore country clothes and kept his ordinary habits.

sentences.zh: 為義季鼓琴，並新聲變曲；

translations.literal: For Yiji he played the zither, including new pieces and variant tunes;
translations.idiomatic: He played the zither for Yiji, including new works and variant melodies;

sentences.zh: 其三調遊弦、廣陵、止息之流，皆與世異。

translations.literal: among them the three modes Wandering Strings, Guangling, and Cease of Breath differed from those in common use.
translations.idiomatic: among them the three pieces Wandering Strings, Guangling, and Cease of Breath differed from common versions.

sentences.zh: 文帝每欲見之，嘗謂黃門侍郎張敷曰：「吾東巡之日，當宴戴公山下也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen often wished to see him and once told the Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Zhang Fu, "On the day I tour east I shall feast below Mount Dai Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen often wished to meet him and once told Zhang Fu, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, "When I journey east I shall hold a feast below Mount Dai Gong.

sentences.zh: 以其好音，長給正聲伎一部。

translations.literal: Because Yong loved music, he was long supplied with a full ensemble of orthodox music.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yong loved music, the court long provided him a full company of court musicians.

sentences.zh: 顒合何嘗、白鵠二聲以為一調，號為清曠。

translations.literal: Yong combined the two pieces He Chang and White Swan into one mode, called Clear and Open.
translations.idiomatic: Yong merged the pieces He Chang and White Swan into a single mode he named Clear and Open.

sentences.zh: 自漢世始有佛像，形制未工，逵特善其事，顒亦參焉。

translations.literal: Since the Han there had been Buddha images, but the forms were not yet refined; Kui was especially skilled in this, and Yong also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha images had existed since Han times but were still crude in form; Kui was especially adept, and Yong assisted him.

sentences.zh: 宋世子鑄丈六銅像於瓦官寺，既成，面恨瘦，工人不能改，乃迎顒看之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent of Song cast a bronze image one zhang six in height at Waguan Monastery; when finished the face seemed too thin and the craftsmen could not amend it — they invited Yong to look.
translations.idiomatic: The Song heir apparent cast a bronze statue one zhang six tall at Waguan Monastery; when it was done the face seemed too lean and artisans could not fix it — they asked Yong to inspect it.
