sentences.zh: 顒曰：「非面瘦，乃臂胛肥耳。」

translations.literal: Yong said, "It is not that the face is thin — the shoulders and upper arms are too full.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "The face is not thin — the shoulders and upper arms are too heavy.

sentences.zh: 及減臂胛，瘦患即除，無不嘆服。

translations.literal: When the shoulders and upper arms were reduced, the defect of thinness vanished; none failed to admire it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the shoulders and arms were slimmed, the face looked right; all marveled at his eye.

sentences.zh: 十八年卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died in the eighteenth year; he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year, leaving no son.

sentences.zh: 景陽山成，顒已亡矣。

translations.literal: When Jingyang Mountain was completed Yong was already gone.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Jingyang Mountain was finished, Yong was already dead.

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「恨不得使戴顒觀之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed, "How I regret that Dai Yong could not see it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "What a pity Dai Yong could not have seen it."

sentences.zh: 翟法賜

translations.literal: Zhai Fasi
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Fasi

sentences.zh: 翟法賜，尋陽柴桑人也。

translations.literal: Zhai Fasi was a native of Chaisang in Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Fasi was from Chaisang in Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖湯，祖莊，父矯，並高尚不仕，逃避徵辟。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tang, grandfather Zhuang, and father Jiao all lived in lofty reclusion and avoided summons.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tang, grandfather Zhuang, and father Jiao were all recluses of high standing who evaded official appointment.

sentences.zh: 法賜少守家業，立室廬山頂。

translations.literal: Fasi in youth kept the family way and built a hut on the summit of Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Fasi upheld the family tradition and built a dwelling on Mount Lu's summit.

sentences.zh: 喪親後，便不復還家，不食五穀，以獸皮及結草為衣，雖鄉親中表莫得見焉。

translations.literal: After his parents' death he never returned home, ate no grain, and wore beast skins and garments woven of grass — even kinsmen and cousins could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his parents he never went home, ate no grain, and clothed himself in hides and grass-woven garments — even kin and cousins could not see him.

sentences.zh: 徵辟一無所就。

translations.literal: He accepted no summons whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no appointment of any kind.

sentences.zh: 後家人至石室尋求，因復遠徙，違避徵聘，遁跡幽深，卒於岩石間。

translations.literal: Later his family came to the stone chamber seeking him; he moved farther away again, evading recruitment, hiding in the deep wilds, and died among the rocks.
translations.idiomatic: When his family later searched for him in his stone cell, he moved still farther off, shunning recruiters and hiding in remote depths until he died among the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 雷次宗

translations.literal: Lei Cizong
translations.idiomatic: Lei Cizong

sentences.zh: 雷次宗，字仲倫，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Lei Cizong, styled Zhonglun, was a native of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Cizong, styled Zhonglun, was from Nanchang in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 少入廬山，事沙門釋慧遠，篤志好學，尤明三禮、毛詩。

translations.literal: In youth he entered Mount Lu to study under the monk Shi Huiyuan; he was devoted to learning and especially versed in the three Rites and the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he went to Mount Lu to study under Huiyuan; devoted to learning, he was especially expert in the three Rites and the Mao Odes.

sentences.zh: 隱退不受徵辟。

translations.literal: He lived in retirement and would not accept summons.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion and refused official appointment.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉十五年，徵至都，開館於雞籠山，聚徒教授，置生百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia he was summoned to the capital; a hall was opened on Cock Cage Mountain to gather pupils and teach — more than a hundred students were enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia he was called to the capital; a school was opened on Cock Cage Mountain where he taught more than a hundred students.

sentences.zh: 會稽朱膺之、潁川庾蔚之並以儒學總監諸生。

translations.literal: Zhu Yingzhi of Kuaiji and Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, both Confucian scholars, supervised the students.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingzhi of Kuaiji and Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, both classicists, oversaw the pupils.

sentences.zh: 時國子學未立，上留意藝文，使丹陽尹何尚之立玄學，太子率更令何承天立史學，司徒參軍謝元立文學，凡四學並建。

translations.literal: The National University had not yet been established; the sovereign attended to literary studies and had He Shangzhi, Governor of Danyang, establish the study of Mysteries; He Chengtian, Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, establish the study of History; Xie Yuan, Staff Officer to the Minister over the Masses, establish the study of Letters — four schools were founded together.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial university did not yet exist; the emperor valued learning and had He Shangzhi establish a school of Mysteries, He Chengtian a school of History, and Xie Yuan a school of Letters — four academies in all.

sentences.zh: 車駕數至次宗館，資給甚厚。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage often came to Cizong's hall and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Cizong's academy and lavished support upon him.

sentences.zh: 久之，還廬山，公卿以下並設祖道。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to Mount Lu; nobles and ministers all held a farewell feast for him.
translations.idiomatic: After a long stay he returned to Mount Lu; officials down to the ministers held a parting banquet.

sentences.zh: 後又征詣都，為築室於鍾山西岩下，謂之招隱館，使為皇太子、諸王講喪服經。

translations.literal: He was summoned again to the capital; a house was built for him on the western cliff of Zhongshan, called the Lodge for Summoning Recluses, and he was charged to lecture the heir apparent and the princes on mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again; a dwelling was built on Zhongshan's western cliff — the Lodge for Summoning Recluses — and he instructed the crown prince and princes in mourning ritual.

sentences.zh: 次宗不入公門，乃使自華林東門入延賢堂就業。

translations.literal: Cizong did not enter the public gate; they had him enter by the east gate of Hualin to teach at the Hall for Extending Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Cizong would not pass through the main gate; he was admitted by Hualin's east gate to teach in the Hall for Extending Worthies.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒於鍾山。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died on Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died on Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 子肅之頗傳其業。

translations.literal: His son Suzhi largely transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Suzhi largely carried on his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 郭希林

translations.literal: Guo Xilin
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xilin

sentences.zh: 郭希林，武昌人也。

translations.literal: Guo Xilin was a native of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xilin was from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖翻，晉世高尚不仕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fan in the Jin era lived in lofty reclusion and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fan in Jin times lived in reclusion and never took office.

sentences.zh: 希林少守家業，徵召一無所就，卒。

translations.literal: Xilin in youth kept the family way; he accepted no summons and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xilin in youth upheld the family tradition, refused every summons, and died.

sentences.zh: 子蒙亦隱居不仕。

translations.literal: His son Meng also lived in reclusion and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: His son Meng likewise lived in seclusion and held no office.

sentences.zh: 劉凝之

translations.literal: Liu Ningzhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ningzhi

sentences.zh: 劉凝之，字隱安，小名長生，南郡枝江人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ningzhi, styled Yin'an, childhood name Changsheng, was a native of Zhijiang in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ningzhi, styled Yin'an, called Changsheng in childhood, was from Zhijiang in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父期公，衡陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Qigong was Governor of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qigong had been Governor of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 兄盛公，高尚不仕。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shenggong lived in lofty reclusion and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shenggong was a recluse who never took office.

sentences.zh: 凝之慕老萊、嚴子陵為人，推家財與弟及兄子，立屋於野外，非其力不食。

translations.literal: Ningzhi admired the conduct of Old Lai and Yan Ziling; he gave the family wealth to his younger brother and his brother's son, built a house in the wilds, and would not eat what his own labor had not provided.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi took Old Lai and Yan Ziling as his models; he gave the family estate to his brother and nephew, built a hut in the wilderness, and ate only what his own hands produced.

sentences.zh: 州裏重其行，辟召一無所就。

translations.literal: The district esteemed his conduct; he accepted no appointment whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: The region honored his way of life; he accepted no summons.

sentences.zh: 妻梁州刺史郭銓女也，遣送豐麗，凝之悉散之屬親。

translations.literal: His wife was a daughter of Guo Quan, Governor of Liangzhou; she was sent off with rich gifts — Ningzhi gave them all to kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a daughter of Guo Quan, Governor of Liangzhou; her dowry was lavish, but Ningzhi distributed it all among relatives.

sentences.zh: 妻亦能不慕榮華，與凝之共居儉苦。

translations.literal: His wife also could disdain glory; with Ningzhi she shared a spare life.
translations.idiomatic: His wife likewise scorned worldly splendor and lived in frugality with him.

sentences.zh: 夫妻共乘蒲笨車，出市買易，周用之外，輒以施人。

translations.literal: Husband and wife together rode a crude rush-woven cart to market to trade; beyond daily needs they always gave the rest away.
translations.idiomatic: Together they drove a rough rush cart to market; whatever exceeded their needs they gave away.

sentences.zh: 為村裏所誣，一年三輸公調，求輒與之。

translations.literal: The village falsely charged him; three times in one year he paid the public levy — whenever they demanded it he gave it.
translations.idiomatic: The village wrongfully taxed him; three times in one year he paid the public levy — whenever they asked, he paid.

sentences.zh: 又嘗有人認其所著屐，笑曰：「僕著已敗，令家中覓新者備君。」

translations.literal: Once someone claimed the clogs he was wearing; he smiled and said, "Mine are already worn out — have your household find new ones for you.
translations.idiomatic: Once a man claimed the clogs on his feet; he smiled and said, "Mine are worn through — let your people find you a new pair.

sentences.zh: 此人後田中得所失屐，送還不肯復取。

translations.literal: Later the man found his lost clogs in the field and returned them; Ningzhi would not take them back.
translations.idiomatic: The man later recovered his own clogs in the fields and tried to return them; Ningzhi would not accept them.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶、衡陽王義季鎮江陵，並遣使存問。

translations.literal: Prince Yiqing of Linchuan and Prince Yiji of Hengyang, holding Jiangling, both sent envoys to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiqing of Linchuan and Prince Yiji of Hengyang, when stationed at Jiangling, both sent messengers to greet him.

sentences.zh: 凝之答書頓首稱僕，不為百姓禮，人或譏焉。

translations.literal: In reply Ningzhi bowed his head and styled himself "your servant," not using the commoner's form — some mocked this.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi's letters bowed and called himself "servant," not using the commoner's style — and some ridiculed him for it.

sentences.zh: 凝之曰：「昔老萊向楚王稱僕，嚴陵亦抗禮光武，未聞巢、許稱臣堯、舜。」

translations.literal: Ningzhi said, "Long ago Old Lai addressed the King of Chu as 'servant'; Yan Ziling also returned Guangwu's courtesies on equal terms — one never heard that Chao and Xu called themselves subjects of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi said, "Old Lai once addressed the King of Chu as 'servant,' and Yan Ziling stood on equal terms with Emperor Guangwu — yet who ever heard that Chao Fu and Xu You styled themselves subjects of Yao and Shun?

sentences.zh: 時戴顒與衡陽王義季書亦稱僕。

translations.literal: At that time Dai Yong in his letter to Prince Yiji of Hengyang also styled himself "servant."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dai Yong likewise signed himself "servant" in writing to Prince Yiji of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 荊州年饑，義季慮凝之餒斃，餉錢十萬。

translations.literal: Jingzhou had famine that year; Yiji feared Ningzhi would starve and sent him a hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Jingzhou that year; Yiji feared Ningzhi might starve and sent a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 凝之大喜，將錢至市門，觀有饑色者悉分與之，俄頃立盡。

translations.literal: Ningzhi was greatly pleased; he took the money to the market gate, saw all who looked hungry and divided it among them — in a moment it was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi was delighted; he carried the money to the market gate, gave it to everyone who looked hungry, and in an instant it was spent.

sentences.zh: 性好山水，一旦攜妻子泛江湖，隱居衡山之陽，登高嶺，絕人跡，為小屋居之。

translations.literal: He loved mountains and waters; one day he took wife and children onto the rivers and lakes, hid on the southern slope of Mount Heng, climbed the high ridge, cut off all human tracks, and lived in a small hut.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape; one day he took wife and children onto the waterways, retired to the southern face of Mount Heng, climbed a high ridge beyond human paths, and dwelt in a small hut.

sentences.zh: 采藥服食，妻子皆從其志。

translations.literal: He gathered herbs and took them for nourishment; wife and children all followed his will.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered medicinal plants for sustenance; his wife and children followed his way.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十九。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 龔祈字孟道，武陵漢壽人也。

translations.literal: Gong Qi, styled Mengdao, was a native of Hanshou in Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Qi, styled Mengdao, was from Hanshou in Wuling.

sentences.zh: 從祖玄之，父黎人，並不應徵辟。

translations.literal: His father's father's cousin Xuanzhi and his father Liren both would not answer summons.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-uncle Xuanzhi and his father Liren both refused official appointment.

sentences.zh: 祈風姿端雅，容止可觀。

translations.literal: Qi's bearing was elegant and dignified; his deportment was admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Qi bore himself with refined grace; his manner was striking.

sentences.zh: 中書郎範述見之歎曰：「此荊楚之仙人也。」

translations.literal: Fan Shu, Secretariat Gentleman, saw him and sighed, "This is an immortal of Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shu, Secretariat Gentleman, saw him and exclaimed, "Here is an immortal of the Jing-Chu lands.

sentences.zh: 自少及長，徵辟一無所就。

translations.literal: From youth to age he accepted no summons.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he accepted no appointment.

sentences.zh: 時或賦詩，而言不及世事。

translations.literal: At times he composed poetry, but his words never touched on worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes wrote verse, but never spoke of public affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒年四十二。

translations.literal: He died at forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 朱百年

translations.literal: Zhu Bainian
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bainian

sentences.zh: 朱百年，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Bainian was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bainian was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖凱之，晉左衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kaizhi was Left Defender General of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kaizhi had been Jin's Left Defender General.

sentences.zh: 父濤，揚州主簿。

translations.literal: His father Tao was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 百年少有高情，親亡服闋，攜妻孔氏入會稽南山，伐樵采箬為業，每以樵箬置道頭，輒為行人所取，明旦已復如此，人稍怪之，積久方知是朱隱士所賣，須者隨其所堪多少，留錢取樵箬而去。

translations.literal: Bainian from youth had lofty feeling; when mourning for his parents ended he took his wife, Lady Kong, into the southern mountains of Kuaiji, felling wood and gathering bamboo leaves for a living. Each day he placed firewood and leaves at the roadside and travelers took them; by the next morning it was the same again. People gradually found it strange; after long acquaintance they learned it was the recluse Zhu selling — buyers left money according to what they took and carried off wood and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bainian cherished high ideals; when mourning ended he took his wife Lady Kong into Kuaiji's southern hills, making a living by cutting firewood and gathering bamboo leaves. Each day he left bundles at the roadside for passersby to take; by morning it was always the same. People grew curious; in time they learned the recluse Zhu was selling — buyers left what they thought fair and carried off wood and leaves.

sentences.zh: 或遇寒雪，樵箬不售，無以自資，輒自榜船送妻還孔氏，天晴迎之。

translations.literal: Sometimes in cold snow when wood and leaves would not sell and he had no means to live, he would pole a boat himself to send his wife back to the Kong family and fetch her again when the weather cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In bitter snow when nothing sold and he could not support himself, he poled his boat to send his wife to her family and brought her back when fair weather returned.

sentences.zh: 有時出山陰為妻買繒采五三尺，好飲酒，遇醉或失之。

translations.literal: At times he came down to Shanyin to buy five or three feet of silk for his wife; he loved wine and when drunk sometimes lost it.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he went to Shanyin to buy silk for his wife; he loved wine and when drunk would sometimes lose it on the way.

sentences.zh: 頗言玄理，時為詩詠，往往有高勝之言。

translations.literal: He often spoke of metaphysics and at times composed verse — often with words of surpassing elevation.
translations.idiomatic: He often discoursed on metaphysics and wrote poems that frequently rose to rare heights.

sentences.zh: 隱跡避人，唯與同縣孔覬友善。

translations.literal: He hid his traces and avoided people; only Kong Yi of his county was his friend.
translations.idiomatic: He hid from the world; only Kong Yi of his district was his close friend.

sentences.zh: 覬亦嗜酒，相得輒酣對盡歡。

translations.literal: Yi also loved wine; when they met they drank face to face in full delight.
translations.idiomatic: Yi too loved wine; when they met they drank together until utterly content.

sentences.zh: 百年室家素貧，母以冬月亡，衣並無絮，自此不衣綿帛。

translations.literal: Bainian's household had always been poor; his mother died in winter and he had no cotton in his clothes — from then on he wore no silk or floss.
translations.idiomatic: Bainian's family had always been poor; his mother died in winter with no cotton padding in her garments — thereafter he wore no silk or padded cloth.

sentences.zh: 嘗寒時就覬宿，衣悉夾布，飲酒醉眠，覬以臥具覆之，百年不覺也。

translations.literal: Once in cold weather he stayed overnight with Yi; his clothes were all of layered cloth; he drank, grew drunk, and slept — Yi covered him with bedding, but Bainian did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Once in cold weather he lodged with Yi wearing only layered cloth; drunk, he fell asleep while Yi covered him with quilts — Bainian never noticed.

sentences.zh: 既覺，引臥具去體，謂覬曰：「綿定奇溫。」

translations.literal: When he awoke he pulled the bedding from his body and said to Yi, "Cotton is wonderfully warm.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke he pushed the covers away and told Yi, "Cotton is marvelously warm.

sentences.zh: 因流涕悲慟，覬亦為之傷感。

translations.literal: He wept in grief; Yi was moved to sorrow as well.
translations.idiomatic: He wept in anguish, and Yi grieved with him.

sentences.zh: 除太子舍人，不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent — he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Attendant of the Heir Apparent but declined.

sentences.zh: 顏竣為東揚州，發教餉百年穀五百斛，不受。

translations.literal: Yan Jun was Eastern Governor of Yangzhou and issued an order sending Bainian five hundred hu of grain — he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun, Eastern Governor of Yangzhou, sent orders gifting Bainian five hundred hu of grain; he refused.

sentences.zh: 時山陰又有寒人姚吟亦有高趣，為衣冠所重。

translations.literal: At that time in Shanyin there was also the poor man Yao Yin, who had lofty tastes and was esteemed by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shanyin also had the poor scholar Yao Yin, a man of elevated spirit whom the gentry respected.

sentences.zh: 竣餉吟米二百斛，吟亦辭之。

translations.literal: Jun sent Yin two hundred hu of rice; Yin also declined.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Yin two hundred hu of rice; Yin likewise refused.

sentences.zh: 百年卒山中。

translations.literal: Bainian died in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Bainian died in the hills.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗為會稽太守，餉百年妻米百斛。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong was Governor of Kuaiji and sent Bainian's wife a hundred hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong, Governor of Kuaiji, sent Bainian's wife a hundred hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 百年妻遣婢詣郡門奉辭固讓，時人美之，以比梁鴻妻。

translations.literal: Bainian's wife sent a maid to the commandery gate with a letter firmly declining; contemporaries praised her, comparing her to the wife of Liang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His wife sent a servant to the commandery gate with a letter of firm refusal; people praised her, likening her to Liang Hong's wife.

sentences.zh: 關康之

translations.literal: Guan Kangzhi
translations.idiomatic: Guan Kangzhi

sentences.zh: 關康之，字伯愉，河東楊人也。

translations.literal: Guan Kangzhi, styled Boyu, was a native of Yang in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Kangzhi, styled Boyu, was from Yang in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世居京口，寓屬南平昌。

translations.literal: His family had long lived in Jingkou and was registered in Nanpingchang.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long resided in Jingkou and was enrolled in Nanpingchang.

sentences.zh: 少而篤學，姿狀豐偉。

translations.literal: From youth he studied earnestly; his stature was tall and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He studied devotedly from youth and was tall and imposing in bearing.

sentences.zh: 下邳趙繹以文義見稱，康之與友善。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi of Xiapi was famed for literary learning; Kangzhi was on friendly terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi of Xiapi was renowned for classical learning; Kangzhi befriended him.

sentences.zh: 特進顏延之等當時名士十許人入山候之，見其散發被黃布帊，席松葉，枕一塊白石而臥，了不相眄。

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi, Special Grand Master, and some ten other eminent men of the day entered the mountain to visit him; they saw him with hair loose, wrapped in yellow cloth, sleeping on pine needles with a block of white stone for a pillow — he did not glance at them at all.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi and some ten celebrated men of the day climbed the mountain to see him; they found him with hair unbound, a yellow cloth about his shoulders, sleeping on pine needles with a white stone for a pillow — he never looked their way.

sentences.zh: 延之等咨嗟而退，不敢幹也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and the others sighed in admiration and withdrew, not daring to intrude.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi and the rest sighed in wonder and withdrew, not daring to disturb him.

sentences.zh: 晉陵顧悅之難王弼易義四十餘條，康之申王難顧，遠有情理。

translations.literal: Gu Yuezhi of Jinling raised more than forty objections to Wang Bi's meanings in the Changes; Kangzhi upheld Wang against Gu — far from lacking reason.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yuezhi of Jinling challenged more than forty points in Wang Bi's commentary on the Changes; Kangzhi defended Wang against Gu with cogent argument.

sentences.zh: 又為毛詩義，經籍疑滯，多所論釋。

translations.literal: He also wrote meanings for the Mao Odes; wherever the classics were doubtful he offered many explanations.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote exegesis on the Mao Odes and clarified many cruxes in the canon.

sentences.zh: 嘗就沙門支僧納學算，妙盡其能。

translations.literal: He once studied computation under the monk Zhi Sengna and mastered it to perfection.
translations.idiomatic: He studied mathematics under the monk Sengna and mastered it completely.

sentences.zh: 徵辟一無所就，棄絕人事，守志閒居。

translations.literal: He accepted no summons, abandoned worldly affairs, and kept his will in quiet retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every appointment, renounced worldly affairs, and lived in tranquil resolve.

sentences.zh: 弟雙之為臧質車騎參軍，與質俱下至赭圻，病卒，瘞于水濱。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shuangzhi was Cavalry Staff Officer to Zang Zhi; he went down with Zhi to Zhuchi, fell ill and died, and was buried on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shuangzhi served Zang Zhi as Cavalry Staff Officer; he accompanied Zhi to Zhuchi, fell ill and died, and was buried by the water.

sentences.zh: 康之時得病小差，牽以迎喪，因得虛勞病，寢頓二十餘年。

translations.literal: Kangzhi was then slightly recovered from illness; he was drawn along to meet the funeral procession and thereby contracted consumption; he lay prostrate more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhi was then slightly improved; drawn out to meet the bier, he contracted consumption and lay bedridden more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 時有閑日，輒臥論文義。

translations.literal: When he had leisure he would lie and discuss literary meanings.
translations.idiomatic: On his better days he would lie abed and discourse on the classics.

sentences.zh: 普明字文達，少就康之受業，至性過人。

translations.literal: Puming, styled Wenda, in youth studied under Kangzhi; his utmost nature surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Puming, styled Wenda, studied under Kangzhi in youth; his filial devotion was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 居貧與兄共處一帳，兄亡，仍以帳施靈。

translations.literal: Living in poverty he shared one canopy with his elder brother; when his brother died he still gave the canopy for the bier.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he shared one canopy with his brother; when his brother died he gave even that canopy for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 蚊甚多，通夕不得寢，而終不道侵螫。

translations.literal: Mosquitoes were many; all night he could not sleep, yet he never spoke of their stings.
translations.idiomatic: Mosquitoes swarmed; he could not sleep all night yet never complained of their bites.

sentences.zh: 僑居會稽，會稽士子高其行，當葬兄，皆送金為贈，後至者不復受。

translations.literal: Living as a sojourner in Kuaiji, the gentlemen of Kuaiji honored his conduct; when burying his brother they all sent gold as gifts — those who came later he would not accept from.
translations.idiomatic: Sojourning in Kuaiji, the local scholars honored him; when he buried his brother they sent gold as gifts — but he refused those who came after the grave was complete.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，答曰：「本以兄墓不周，故不逆親友之意。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason he replied, "At first the tomb was not complete, so I did not go against friends and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "At first my brother's tomb was unfinished, so I did not refuse friends and kin.

sentences.zh: 今實己足，豈可利亡者餘贈邪。」

translations.literal: Now it is truly enough — how could one profit from what remains for the dead?
translations.idiomatic: Now it is truly sufficient — how could I profit from gifts meant for the dead?

sentences.zh: 齊豫章王嶷為揚州，徵為議曹從事，不就。

translations.literal: Prince Liao of Yuzhang in Qi was Governor of Yangzhou and summoned him as Retainer in the Discussion Bureau — he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liao of Yuzhang, Governor of Yangzhou under Qi, summoned him as Discussion Bureau Retainer; he declined.

sentences.zh: 惠明字智遠，立性貞固，有道術。

translations.literal: Huiming, styled Zhiyuan, was upright and firm by nature and possessed the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Huiming, styled Zhiyuan, was steadfast by nature and versed in the Way.

sentences.zh: 居金華山，舊多毒害，自惠明居之，無復辛螫之苦。

translations.literal: He lived on Mount Jinhua, where poisons had long been many; from the time Huiming dwelt there, the bitter sting of insects was no more.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on Mount Jinhua, once rife with venomous creatures; after Huiming settled there, stinging pests troubled the place no more.

sentences.zh: 藏名匿跡，人莫之知。

translations.literal: He hid his name and concealed his traces; no one knew of him.
translations.idiomatic: He concealed his name and tracks; none knew who he was.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝召不至，齊高帝征又不至。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song summoned him — he did not come; Emperor Gao of Qi summoned him again — he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song summoned him in vain; Emperor Gao of Qi summoned him again — he would not come.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子在東宮，苦延方至，仍又辭歸。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui in the Eastern Palace pressed him hard to come; when he arrived he again asked leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhui at the Eastern Palace urged him repeatedly; when he came he soon asked to return.

sentences.zh: 俄自金華輕棹西下，及就路，回之豐安。

translations.literal: Before long he lightly poled west from Jinhua; when he had set out on the road he turned back to Feng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he poled lightly down from Jinhua; on the road he turned back to Feng'an.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，唐宇之祅賊入城塗地，唯豐安獨全，時人以為有先覺。

translations.literal: Within ten days the demonic rebels of Tang Yu entered the city and smeared the ground with blood — only Feng'an remained whole; contemporaries thought he had foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the rebel Tang Yu's forces entered the city and slaughtered without mercy — only Feng'an was spared; people said he had foreseen it.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝敕為立館。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi ordered a lodge built for him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi ordered a residence built for him.

sentences.zh: 漁父者，不知姓名，亦不知何許人也。

translations.literal: The Fisherman — his name is unknown, and it is not known whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: The Fisherman — neither his name nor his origin is known.

sentences.zh: 太康孫緬為尋陽太守，落日逍遙渚際，見一輕舟陵波隱顯。

translations.literal: Sun Mian of Taikang was Governor of Xunyang; at sunset he wandered by the islets and saw a light skiff riding the waves, now hidden, now shown.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian of Taikang was Governor of Xunyang; at dusk he strolled the shoals and saw a light boat cresting the waves, now visible, now lost.

sentences.zh: 俄而漁父至，神韻蕭灑，垂綸長嘯，緬甚異之。

translations.literal: Before long the fisherman came; his spirit was lofty and free, he let down his line and sang long — Mian found it very strange.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the fisherman arrived — bearing at ease, line cast, singing long; Mian was deeply struck.

sentences.zh: 乃問：「有魚賣乎？」

translations.literal: He then asked, "Have you fish to sell?
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "Do you have fish to sell?

sentences.zh: 漁父笑而答曰：「其釣非釣，寧賣魚者邪？」

translations.literal: The fisherman smiled and replied, "My angling is not angling — would I be one who sells fish?
translations.idiomatic: The fisherman smiled and said, "This fishing is not fishing — would I be a man who sells fish?"

sentences.zh: 緬益怪焉。

translations.literal: Mian was all the more astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was still more astonished.

sentences.zh: 遂褰裳涉水，謂曰：「竊觀先生有道者也，終朝鼓枻，良亦勞止。

translations.literal: He then lifted his robe and waded through the water, saying, "I have observed, sir, that you are a man of the Way; to beat the oar all morning is indeed labor.
translations.idiomatic: He waded through the water, saying, "I see you are a man of the Way; to ply the oar from morning on is hard labor indeed.

sentences.zh: 吾聞黃金白璧，重利也，駟馬高蓋，榮勢也。

translations.literal: I have heard that gold and white jade are heavy profit, and four-horse chariots with high canopies are glorious power.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and white jade, I hear, are great profit; teams of four with high canopies are glorious rank.

sentences.zh: 今方王道文明，守在海外，隱鱗之士，靡然向風。

translations.literal: Now the kingly Way is civilized and bright, and guardians are beyond the seas; hidden-scale gentlemen turn to the wind as one.
translations.idiomatic: The royal Way is now bright and civilized, guardians stand beyond the seas, and hidden men of talent turn homeward like grass in the wind.

sentences.zh: 子胡不贊緝熙之美，何晦用其若是也？

translations.literal: Why do you not praise the beauty of radiant peace — why hide yourself so?
translations.idiomatic: Why not lend your voice to this radiant age — why seclude yourself thus?

sentences.zh: 「漁父曰：「僕山海狂人，不達世務，未辨賤貧，無論榮貴。」

translations.literal: The fisherman said, "I am a madman of mountains and seas, ignorant of worldly affairs, unable to distinguish base from rich, let alone honor from glory.
translations.idiomatic: The fisherman said, "I am a madman of mountain and sea, unversed in the world, unable to tell poor from rich — how should I weigh honor against glory?"

sentences.zh: 乃歌曰：「竹竿籊籊，河水浟浟。

translations.literal: He then sang: "Bamboo poles, tall and slender; river waters, broad and flowing.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sang: "Bamboo poles, tall and slender; river waters, broad and flowing.

sentences.zh: 相忘為樂，貪餌吞鉤。

translations.literal: To forget each other is joy; greedy for bait, one swallows the hook.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual forgetting is our joy; greedy for bait, one swallows the hook.

sentences.zh: 非夷非惠，聊以忘憂。」

translations.literal: Neither Bo Yi nor Hui Shi — for a time, to forget care.
translations.idiomatic: Neither recluse nor sophist — only to lay care aside for a while."

sentences.zh: 於是悠然鼓棹而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he leisurely beat the oar and went away.
translations.idiomatic: With that he leisurely poled away.

sentences.zh: 緬字伯緒，太子僕興曾之子也。

translations.literal: Mian, styled Boxu, was son of Xing, Director of the Palace Servants.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, styled Boxu, was son of Xing, Director of the Palace Servants.

sentences.zh: 有學義，宋明帝甚知之。

translations.literal: He had learning and principles; Emperor Ming of Song knew him well.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and principled; Emperor Ming of Song held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 位尚書左丞，東中郎司馬。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Staff Officer to the Eastern Palace General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Staff Officer to the Eastern Palace General.

sentences.zh: 褚伯玉

translations.literal: Chu Boyu
translations.idiomatic: Chu Boyu

sentences.zh: 褚伯玉，字元璩，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Chu Boyu, styled Yuanqu, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Boyu, styled Yuanqu, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖含，始平太守。

translations.literal: His ancestor Han was Governor of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Han had been Governor of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 父逿，征虜參軍。

translations.literal: His father Dao was Staff Officer to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao was Staff Officer to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 伯玉少有隱操，寡欲。

translations.literal: Boyu from youth had a reclusive character and few desires.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Boyu lived reclusively and desired little.

sentences.zh: 年十八，父為之昏。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, his father arranged a marriage for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was eighteen, his father arranged his marriage.

sentences.zh: 婦入前門，伯玉從後門出。

translations.literal: When the bride entered the front gate, Boyu went out the back gate.
translations.idiomatic: As his bride came in the front door, Boyu slipped out the back.

sentences.zh: 遂往剡，居瀑布山。

translations.literal: He then went to Shan, dwelling on Waterfall Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Shan and made his home on Waterfall Mountain.

sentences.zh: 性耐寒暑，時人比之王仲都。

translations.literal: By nature he endured cold and heat; men of the time compared him to Wang Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: He bore cold and heat with ease, and contemporaries likened him to Wang Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 在山三十餘年，隔絕人物。

translations.literal: On the mountain for more than thirty years, he cut himself off from other people.
translations.idiomatic: For over thirty years on the mountain he kept apart from the world.

sentences.zh: 王僧達為吳郡，苦禮致之，伯玉不得已，停郡信宿，才交數言而退。

translations.literal: Wang Sengda, as governor of Wu Commandery, earnestly sought him with ceremony; Boyu had no choice but to stay in the commandery seat for a night or two, exchanged only a few words, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda, as governor of Wu, pressed him with repeated invitations until Boyu could refuse no longer. He lodged at the prefectural seat for a night or two, spoke a few words, and left.

sentences.zh: 甯朔將軍丘珍孫與僧達書曰：「聞褚先生出居貴館，此子滅景雲棲，不事王侯，抗高木食，有年載矣。

translations.literal: General Ning Shuo Qiu Zhensun wrote to Sengda: "I hear that Master Chu has come to lodge at your honored residence. This man has long hidden his light among the clouds, serving neither kings nor marquises, living on lofty trees and coarse food, for many years.
translations.idiomatic: General Ning Shuo Qiu Zhensun wrote to Sengda: "I hear Master Chu is staying at your residence. For years this man has lived apart from the world—refusing kings and lords, eating from the wild and dwelling in the heights.

sentences.zh: 自非折節好賢，何以致之。

translations.literal: Unless one bends his will to honor the worthy, how could one bring him here?
translations.idiomatic: Unless you had humbled yourself to win a recluse, how could he have come?

sentences.zh: 昔文舉棲冶城，安道入昌門，於茲而三焉。

translations.literal: In old times Kong Wenju dwelt on Ye City, and Dai Andao entered Chang Gate—now there are three such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Kong Wenju lived on Ye City and Dai Andao entered Chang Gate—yours makes a third such tale.

sentences.zh: 卻粒之士，餐霞之人，乃可暫致，不宜久羈。

translations.literal: Men who eschew grain and feast on mist may be summoned for a time; they should not be detained long.
translations.idiomatic: A man who lives on dew and forgoes grain may visit briefly; he ought not be held too long.

sentences.zh: 君當思遂其高步，成其羽化。

translations.literal: You should consider letting him resume his lofty steps and complete his transformation into an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: You should help him resume his lofty path and achieve his ascension.

sentences.zh: 望其還策之日，暫紆清塵，亦願助為譬說。」

translations.literal: When he returns with his staff, if you would briefly clear the dust of office, I too would gladly help persuade him."
translations.idiomatic: When he takes up his staff again, clear your official dust for a moment if you can—I will gladly add my own persuasion."

sentences.zh: 僧達答曰：「褚先生從白雲遊舊矣。

translations.literal: Sengda replied: "Master Chu has long roamed the white clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda answered: "Master Chu has wandered among white clouds for years.

sentences.zh: 古之逸人，或留慮兒女，或使華陰成市，而此子索然，唯朋松石，介於孤峰絕嶺者，積數十載。

translations.literal: The recluses of antiquity sometimes kept wives and children in mind, or made Mount Hua into a marketplace; yet this man is utterly bare, keeping only pines and rocks as companions, dwelling between lone peaks and sheer ridges for decades.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient recluses sometimes troubled over wives and children, or turned Mount Hua into a market; this man is utterly bare—only pines and rocks for company—on isolated peaks for decades.

sentences.zh: 近故要其來此，冀慰日夜。

translations.literal: Recently I therefore invited him here, hoping to comfort my days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: I recently asked him here, hoping his presence would ease my loneliness.

sentences.zh: 比談討芝桂，借訪荔蘿，若已窺煙液，臨滄洲矣。

translations.literal: We have lately discussed orchid and cassia, borrowing talk of vines and moss—as if already glimpsing the misted waters and facing the isles of the sea.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately spoken of herbs and hills as though already gazing on misted seas and distant isles.

sentences.zh: 知君欲見之，輒當申譬。」

translations.literal: Knowing that you wish to see him, I shall certainly convey your message."
translations.idiomatic: Since I know you wish to see him, I will certainly pass on your words."

sentences.zh: 顧歡，字景怡，一字玄平，吳郡鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Gu Huan, styled Jingyi, also styled Xuanping, was a man of Yanguan in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Huan, courtesy name Jingyi and also called Xuanping, was from Yanguan in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世寒賤，父祖並為農夫，歡獨好學。

translations.literal: His family for generations was poor and lowly; father and grandfather were both farmers; Huan alone delighted in learning.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been poor; father and grandfather were farmers, but Huan alone loved study.

sentences.zh: 年六七歲，知推六甲。

translations.literal: At six or seven years he could calculate the sexagenary cycle.
translations.idiomatic: At six or seven he could work the sexagenary cycle.

sentences.zh: 家貧，父使田中驅雀，歡作黃雀賦而歸，雀食稻過半。

translations.literal: The family was poor; his father sent him to the fields to drive off sparrows; Huan composed an Ode to the Yellow Sparrow and returned, and the sparrows had eaten more than half the rice.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as they were, his father sent him to scare birds from the fields. Huan wrote an Ode to the Yellow Sparrow and came home—by then the birds had eaten more than half the crop.

sentences.zh: 父怒欲撻之，見賦乃止。

translations.literal: His father in anger was about to beat him, but seeing the ode he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His father was about to thrash him, but read the ode and stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 鄉中有學舍，歡貧無以受業，於舍壁後倚聽，無遺忘者。

translations.literal: In the village there was a schoolhouse; Huan was too poor to receive instruction and leaned against the wall behind the school to listen, forgetting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: A village school stood nearby. Too poor to enroll, he listened from behind the wall and forgot nothing he heard.

sentences.zh: 夕則然松節讀書，或然糠自照。

translations.literal: At night he would burn pine knots to read by, or sometimes burn chaff to light himself.
translations.idiomatic: At night he read by pine-knot fire, or sometimes by the light of burning chaff.

sentences.zh: 及長，篤志不倦。

translations.literal: When grown, his devoted purpose never wearied.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured, his zeal for learning never flagged.

sentences.zh: 聞吳興東遷邵玄之能傳五經文句，假為書師，從之受業。

translations.literal: Hearing that Shao Xuanzhi of Dongqian in Wu Commandery could transmit the phrasing of the Five Classics, he pretended to be a letter-copyist and received instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Shao Xuanzhi of Dongqian could teach the phrasing of the Five Classics, he posed as a copyist and studied under him.

sentences.zh: 同郡顧顗之臨縣，見而異之，遣諸子與游，及孫憲之並受經焉。

translations.literal: Gu Yan of the same commandery, on taking office as magistrate, saw him and marveled, sending his sons to study with him; Sun Xianzhi also received the classics from him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Yan of the same commandery became magistrate, he was struck by Huan and sent his sons to study with him; Sun Xianzhi received the classics from him as well.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，更從豫章雷次宗諮玄儒諸義。

translations.literal: Past twenty he went again to Lei Cizong of Yuzhang to inquire into the various meanings of the mysterious learning.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties he went to Lei Cizong in Yuzhang to pursue the subtler meanings of the learning.

sentences.zh: 母亡，水漿不入口六七日，廬於墓次，遂隱不仕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he took no water or broth for six or seven days, built a hut by the tomb, and thereafter lived in seclusion without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he took no food or drink for six or seven days, lodged by her tomb, and thereafter lived apart from office.

sentences.zh: 於剡天臺山開館聚徒，受業者常近百人。

translations.literal: On Mount Tiantai in Shan he opened a lodge and gathered disciples; those receiving instruction were often nearly a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Tiantai in Shan he opened a school; nearly a hundred students studied with him.

sentences.zh: 歡早孤，讀詩至「哀哀父母」，輒執書慟泣，由是受學者廢蓼莪篇，不復講焉。

translations.literal: Huan was orphaned early; reading the Odes to the line "Alas, alas, my parents," he would seize the book and weep; for this reason his students abandoned the Laolai chapter and no longer lectured on it.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he wept whenever he reached "Alas, alas, my parents" in the Odes. His students therefore dropped the Laolai chapter and would not teach it.

sentences.zh: 晚節服食，不與人通。

translations.literal: In his later years he took elixirs and did not mingle with others.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he took elixirs and kept apart from others.

sentences.zh: 每旦出戶，山鳥集其掌取食。

translations.literal: Each morning when he went out his door, mountain birds would gather on his palm to take food.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning when he stepped outside, mountain birds alighted on his palm to be fed.

sentences.zh: 好黃、老，通解陰陽書，為數術多效驗。

translations.literal: He favored Huang-Lao thought, thoroughly understood books on yin and yang, and his numerological arts often proved effective.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Huang-Lao teaching, mastered yin-yang lore, and his divinations often came true.

sentences.zh: 初以元嘉中出都，寄住東府。

translations.literal: At first in the Yuanjia era he went to the capital and lodged in the Eastern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanjia era he went to the capital and lodged in the Eastern Residence.

sentences.zh: 忽題柱云：「三十年二月二十一日」，因東歸。

translations.literal: Suddenly he wrote on a pillar: "The thirtieth year, second month, twenty-first day," and then returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he wrote on a pillar, "Year 30, second month, twenty-first day," and returned east.

sentences.zh: 後元凶弑逆，是其年月日也。

translations.literal: Later the crown prince committed regicide—it was indeed that year, month, and day.
translations.idiomatic: Later the crown prince murdered his father—it was indeed that year, month, and day.

sentences.zh: 弟子鮑靈綬門前有一株樹，大十餘圍，上有精魅，數見影。

translations.literal: Before the door of his disciple Bao Ling's house stood a tree more than ten arm-spans around; on it was a spirit that often showed its shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Before his disciple Bao Ling's door stood a tree more than ten arm-spans around, haunted by a spirit that often cast a shadow.

sentences.zh: 歡印樹，樹即枯死。

translations.literal: Huan stamped the tree, and the tree at once withered and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huan stamped the tree, and it withered at once.

sentences.zh: 山陰白石村多邪病，村人告訴求哀，歡往村中為講老子，規地作獄。

translations.literal: In Baishi Village, Shanyin, there were many evil illnesses; villagers appealed to him for mercy; Huan went to the village to expound Laozi and marked out ground for a prison.
translations.idiomatic: Baishi Village in Shanyin suffered many demonic afflictions. Villagers begged his aid; he went there, expounded Laozi, and marked out ground for a spirit-prison.

sentences.zh: 有頃，見狐狸黿鼉自入獄中者甚多，即命殺之。

translations.literal: Before long he saw many foxes, turtles, and crocodiles enter the prison of themselves; he then ordered them killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon foxes, turtles, and crocodiles filed into the prison of their own accord; he had them killed.

sentences.zh: 病者皆愈。

translations.literal: The sick all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The afflicted all recovered.

sentences.zh: 又有病邪者問歡，歡曰：「家有何書？

translations.literal: There was also one afflicted by evil who asked Huan; Huan said: "What books are in your house?
translations.idiomatic: Another man possessed by evil spirits asked Huan for help. Huan said, "What books do you keep at home?

sentences.zh: 「答曰：「唯有孝經而已。」

translations.literal: " He answered: "Only the Classic of Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Only the Classic of Filial Piety."

sentences.zh: 歡曰：「可取仲尼居置病人枕邊恭敬之，自差也。」

translations.literal: Huan said: "Take the chapter 'Confucius at Rest' and place it by the sick man's pillow with reverence—he will recover of himself."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Place the chapter 'Confucius at Rest' beside the patient's pillow with reverence. He will recover."

sentences.zh: 而後病者果愈。

translations.literal: And afterward the sick man indeed recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The man did recover.

sentences.zh: 後人問其故，答曰：「善禳惡，正勝邪，此病者所以差也。」

translations.literal: When later men asked the reason, he answered: "Good exorcises evil; correctness overcomes perversity—this is why the sick recovered."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Good drives out evil; the upright defeats the crooked—that is why they were healed."

sentences.zh: 齊高帝輔政，徵為揚州主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted in government, Huan was summoned as Registrar of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi was regent, Huan was summoned as Registrar of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼乃至，稱「山谷臣顧歡上表」，進政綱一卷。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne and thereafter, he styled himself "Your subject of the valleys, Gu Huan," and presented a memorial and a scroll on government principles.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao took the throne, Huan styled himself "Gu Huan, subject of the valleys" and submitted a memorial with a chapter on statecraft.

sentences.zh: 時員外郎劉思效表陳讜言，優詔並稱美之。

translations.literal: At the time the Outer Gentleman Liu Sixiao memorialized with forthright words; an excellent edict praised them both.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sixiao, Outer Gentleman, also submitted frank counsel; an edict praised them both.

sentences.zh: 歡東歸，上賜麈尾、素琴。

translations.literal: Huan returned east; the emperor bestowed on him a fly-whisk and a plain zither.
translations.idiomatic: Huan returned east; the emperor gave him a fly-whisk and a plain zither.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，詔徵為太學博士，同郡顧黯為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming an edict summoned him as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; Gu An of the same commandery was appointed Gentleman Attendant at Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming's first year an edict summoned him as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; Gu An of the same commandery became Gentleman Attendant at Leisure.

sentences.zh: 黯字長孺，有隱操，與歡不就征。

translations.literal: An, styled Changru, had a reclusive character and, like Huan, did not accept the summons.
translations.idiomatic: An, styled Changru, shared Huan's reclusive bent; neither accepted office.

sentences.zh: 會稽孔珪嘗登嶺尋歡，共談四本。

translations.literal: Kong Gui of Kuaiji once climbed a ridge to seek Huan, and together they discussed the Four Roots.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui of Kuaiji once climbed the hills to visit Huan, and they debated the Four Roots.

sentences.zh: 歡曰：「蘭石危而密，宣國安而疏，士季似而非，公深謬而是。

translations.literal: Huan said: "Lanshi is perilous yet dense, Xuanguo is secure yet loose, Shiji seems right but is not, Gong Shen is mistaken yet is right.
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Lanshi is perilous yet dense; Xuanguo is secure yet loose; Shiji seems right but is not; Gong Shen is wrong yet is right.

sentences.zh: 總而言之，其失則同；

translations.literal: Speaking of them in general, their errors are the same;
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, their errors are the same;

sentences.zh: 曲而辯之，其塗則異。

translations.literal: examined in detail, their paths differ.
translations.idiomatic: examined closely, their paths diverge.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 同昧其本而競談其末，猶未識辰緯而意斷南北。

translations.literal: They alike obscure the root yet compete in discussing the branches, like not knowing the constellations yet presuming to fix north and south.
translations.idiomatic: They alike miss the root yet wrangle over branches—like fixing north and south without knowing the stars.

sentences.zh: 群迷暗爭，失得無准，情長則申，意短則屈。

translations.literal: The crowd, lost in darkness, wrangle; gain and loss have no standard; where feeling runs long they extend, where intent is short they contract.
translations.idiomatic: The lost wrangle in the dark with no measure of truth; passion stretches their case, brevity shrinks it.

sentences.zh: 所以四本並通，莫能相塞。

translations.literal: Therefore the Four Roots all pass through yet none can block the others.
translations.idiomatic: Thus all Four Roots seem to hold, yet none can shut out the rest.

sentences.zh: 夫中理唯一，豈容有二？

translations.literal: The central principle is unique—how could it admit two?
translations.idiomatic: Truth is one—how could there be two?

sentences.zh: 四本無正，失中故也。」

translations.literal: The Four Roots have no true center because they miss the center."
translations.idiomatic: The Four Roots lack a true center because they have lost it."

sentences.zh: 於是著三名論以正之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the Treatise on the Three Names to correct them.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote the Treatise on the Three Names to set them right.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉澄、臨川王常侍朱廣之，並立論難，與之往復；

translations.literal: Minister Liu Cheng and Regular Attendant Zhu Guangzhi of the Prince of Linchuan all set forth treatises to dispute him, and exchanged arguments with him;
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Cheng and Zhu Guangzhi, Regular Attendant to the Prince of Linchuan, wrote treatises against him and debated back and forth;

sentences.zh: 而廣之才理尤精詣也。

translations.literal: yet Guangzhi's literary reasoning was especially penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: but Guangzhi's reasoning was especially keen.

sentences.zh: 廣之字處深，吳郡錢唐人也，善清言。

translations.literal: Guangzhi, styled Chushen, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery and excelled in pure discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi, styled Chushen, was from Qiantang in Wu and excelled at pure talk.

sentences.zh: 初，歡以佛道二家教異，學者互相非毀，乃著夷夏論曰：夫辯是與非，宜據聖典。

translations.literal: At first, because the teachings of Daoism and Buddhism differed and scholars slandered one another, Huan composed the Treatise on Barbarian and Chinese, saying: To distinguish right and wrong, one should rely on the sacred canon.
translations.idiomatic: Because Daoist and Buddhist teachings differed and scholars attacked one another, Huan wrote the Treatise on Barbarian and Chinese: "To judge right and wrong one must appeal to sacred texts.

sentences.zh: 道經云：「老子入關之天竺維衛國，國王夫人名曰淨妙，老子因其晝寢，乘日精入淨妙口中，後年四月八日夜半時，剖右腋而生。

translations.literal: The Daoist classic says: "Laozi, on entering the Pass, went to Kapilavastu in the land of Vaiśālī; the king's consort was named Pure Excellence; because Laozi took a nap by day, he entered her mouth on the sun's essence; in the fourth month, on the eighth night at midnight, he was born from her right armpit.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist scripture says: "Laozi, entering the Pass, went to Kapilavastu in Vaiśālī; the queen-consort Pure Excellence slept by day; he entered her mouth on a sunbeam; on the eighth night of the fourth month he was born from her right armpit.

sentences.zh: 墜地即行七步，於是佛道興焉。」

translations.literal: Falling to earth he walked seven steps at once; thus the Buddhist Way arose."
translations.idiomatic: He fell to earth and walked seven steps at once—thus Buddhism arose."

sentences.zh: 此出玄妙內篇。

translations.literal: This comes from the Inner Chapter of Mystery and Wonder.
translations.idiomatic: This is from the Inner Chapter of Mystery and Wonder.

sentences.zh: 佛經云：「釋迦成佛，有塵劫之數」，出法華無量壽。

translations.literal: The Buddhist sutra says: "Śākyamuni's becoming Buddha spans dust-kalpas in number," from the Lotus and Infinite Life.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist sutra says, "Śākyamuni's buddhahood spans dust-kalpas," from the Lotus and Infinite Life sutras.

sentences.zh: 或「為國師道士，儒林之宗」。

translations.literal: Or "he was National Teacher and Daoist master, patriarch of the Confucian grove."
translations.idiomatic: Or that he was "National Teacher, Daoist master, patriarch of the Confucian grove."

sentences.zh: 出瑞應本起。

translations.literal: This comes from the Responses and Origins.
translations.idiomatic: This is from Responses and Origins.

sentences.zh: 歡論之曰：五帝三皇，不聞有佛；

translations.literal: Huan argued: The Five Emperors and Three August Ones never heard of the Buddha;
translations.idiomatic: Huan argued: The Five Emperors and Three August Ones never heard of Buddha;

sentences.zh: 國師道士，無過老、莊；

translations.literal: as National Teacher and Daoist master, none surpass Laozi and Zhuangzi;
translations.idiomatic: as National Teacher none surpass Laozi and Zhuangzi;

sentences.zh: 儒林之宗，孰出周、孔。

translations.literal: as patriarch of the Confucian grove, who exceeds Zhou and Confucius?
translations.idiomatic: as Confucian patriarch, who exceeds Zhou and Confucius?

sentences.zh: 若孔、老非聖，誰則當之？

translations.literal: If Confucius and Laozi are not sages, who then qualifies?
translations.idiomatic: If Confucius and Laozi are not sages, who is?

sentences.zh: 然二經所說，如合符契。

translations.literal: Yet what the two scriptures say fits like tally-sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the two scriptures say matches like tally-sticks.

sentences.zh: 道則佛也，佛則道也，其聖則符，其跡則反。

translations.literal: The Way is the Buddha, the Buddha is the Way; in sainthood they tally, in traces they diverge.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is Buddha, Buddha is the Way; in holiness they agree, in footprints they differ.

sentences.zh: 或和光以明近，或曜靈以示遠。

translations.literal: Sometimes they blend their light to illumine the near, sometimes they display their spirit to show the far.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they soften their radiance for the near, sometimes blaze forth for the far.

sentences.zh: 道濟天下，故無方而不入，智周萬物，故無物而不為。

translations.literal: The Way saves the world, therefore it enters without fixed direction; wisdom encompasses the myriad things, therefore nothing lies outside its doing.
translations.idiomatic: The Way saves the world and enters everywhere; wisdom embraces all things and leaves nothing undone.

sentences.zh: 其入不同，其為必異，各成其性，不易其事。

translations.literal: Their entry differs, their doing must differ; each completes its nature, unchanging its task.
translations.idiomatic: Their entry differs, their work must differ; each fulfills its nature without changing its charge.

sentences.zh: 是以端委搢紳，諸華之容；

translations.literal: Therefore the upright cap and girdled sash are the bearing of the Hua;
translations.idiomatic: Thus court robes and girdled sashes are the bearing of the Hua;

sentences.zh: 剪發曠衣，群夷之服。

translations.literal: shorn hair and flowing robes are the garb of the many Yi.
translations.idiomatic: shorn hair and flowing robes are the dress of the Yi.

sentences.zh: 擎跽罄折，侯甸之恭；

translations.literal: Kneeling upright and bowing low are the courtesy of marquis and district;
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling upright and bowing deep are the courtesy of lords and vassals;

sentences.zh: 狐蹲狗踞，荒流之肅。

translations.literal: crouching like fox or dog is the solemnity of the wild frontier.
translations.idiomatic: crouching like fox or dog is the solemnity of the frontier wilds.

sentences.zh: 棺殯槨葬，中夏之風；

translations.literal: Coffin, bier, inner and outer coffins are the custom of central Hua;
translations.idiomatic: Coffin, bier, and nested cases are central Hua custom;

sentences.zh: 火焚水沈，西戎之俗。

translations.literal: burning by fire or sinking in water are the ways of the western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: burning or sinking the body are western Rong ways.

sentences.zh: 全形守禮，繼善之教；

translations.literal: Keeping the body whole and observing ritual is the teaching of continuing goodness;
translations.idiomatic: Keeping the body whole and observing rites teaches continuing goodness;

sentences.zh: 毀貌易性，絕惡之學。

translations.literal: destroying the countenance and changing the nature is the learning of cutting off evil.
translations.idiomatic: destroying the countenance and changing nature is the learning of cutting off evil.

sentences.zh: 豈伊同人，爰及異物，鳥王獸長，往往是佛。

translations.literal: How could it be the same people, reaching to different creatures—bird-kings and beast-chiefs are often buddhas.
translations.idiomatic: How could the same people reach different creatures—bird-kings and beast-lords are often called buddhas.

sentences.zh: 無窮世界，聖人代興，或昭五典，或布三乘。

translations.literal: In endless worlds sages arise in turn, sometimes displaying the Five Canons, sometimes spreading the Three Vehicles.
translations.idiomatic: In endless worlds sages arise in turn, sometimes expounding the Five Canons, sometimes spreading the Three Vehicles.

sentences.zh: 在鳥而鳥鳴，在獸而獸吼，教華而華言，化夷而夷語耳。

translations.literal: Among birds the birds cry, among beasts the beasts roar; teaching Hua, Hua speech; transforming Yi, Yi words.
translations.idiomatic: Among birds birds sing, among beasts beasts roar; among Hua, Hua speech; among Yi, Yi words.

sentences.zh: 雖舟車均於致遠，而有川陸之節，佛道齊乎達化，而有夷夏之別。

translations.literal: Though boat and carriage alike reach far, yet there are rules for river and land; though Buddha and Way alike achieve transformation, yet there is distinction between Yi and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Boat and carriage both reach far, yet river and land have their rules; Buddha and Way both transform, yet Yi and Hua differ.

sentences.zh: 若謂其致既均，其法可換者，而車可涉川，舟可行陸乎？

translations.literal: If one says their reach is already equal and their methods interchangeable, can a carriage cross a river, or a boat travel on land?
translations.idiomatic: If their reach is equal and methods interchangeable, can carriages cross rivers or boats run on land?

sentences.zh: 今以中夏之性，效西戎之法，既不全同，又不全異。

translations.literal: Now with the nature of central Hua to imitate western Rong methods—neither wholly the same nor wholly different.
translations.idiomatic: Now central Hua imitates western Rong ways—neither wholly same nor wholly different.

sentences.zh: 下棄妻孥，上絕宗祀。

translations.literal: Below they abandon wife and children; above they cut off ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Below they abandon wives and children; above they sever ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 嗜欲之物，皆以禮伸，孝敬之典，獨以法屈。

translations.literal: Objects of desire are all extended by ritual, yet the canon of filial respect alone is bent by law.
translations.idiomatic: Desire is restrained by ritual everywhere, yet filial piety alone is bent by monastic law.

sentences.zh: 悖禮犯順，曾莫之覺，弱喪忘歸，孰識其舊。

translations.literal: Perversity against ritual and obedience to wrong—none awaken to it; the weak lose their home and forget return—who knows the old way?
translations.idiomatic: They rebel against ritual yet never wake; orphans forget the way home—who remembers the old path?

sentences.zh: 且理之可貴者道也，事之可賤者俗也，舍華效夷，義將安取？

translations.literal: What is precious in principle is the Way; what is base in affairs is custom—abandoning Hua to imitate Yi, where will righteousness be found?
translations.idiomatic: In principle the Way is precious; in practice custom is base—abandoning Hua for Yi, where does righteousness lie?

sentences.zh: 若以道邪？

translations.literal: If by the Way?
translations.idiomatic: If you mean the Way?

sentences.zh: 道固符合矣。

translations.literal: The Way indeed accords.
translations.idiomatic: The Way indeed accords.

sentences.zh: 若以俗邪？

translations.literal: If by custom?
translations.idiomatic: If you mean custom?

sentences.zh: 俗則大乖矣。

translations.literal: Custom then greatly errs.
translations.idiomatic: Custom then errs greatly.

sentences.zh: 屢見刻舷沙門，守株道士，交諍小大，互相彈射。

translations.literal: Repeatedly one sees monks who notch the boat's side and Daoists who guard the stump, wrangling over great and small, shooting at one another.
translations.idiomatic: Monks notch the boat's gunwale and Daoists guard the tree stump, wrangling and shooting barbs at each other.

sentences.zh: 或域道以為兩，或混俗以為一，是牽異以為同，破同以為異，則乖爭之由，淆亂之本也。

translations.literal: Some fence off the Way as two, some mix custom as one—this is forcing difference into sameness, breaking sameness into difference; the source of strife and the root of confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Some fence the Way as two, some melt custom into one—forcing difference into sameness, breaking sameness into difference: the root of strife.

sentences.zh: 尋聖道雖同，而法有左右，始乎無端，終乎無末，泥洹仙化，各是一術。

translations.literal: Seeking the sage Way, though the same, the methods have left and right; beginning without source, ending without tip; nirvana and immortal transformation are each a technique.
translations.idiomatic: The sage Way is one, yet methods have left and right; beginning without source, ending without end—nirvana and immortal transformation are each a path.

sentences.zh: 佛號正真，道稱正一，一歸無死，真會無生。

translations.literal: The Buddha is called True Correctness, the Way is called Correct Unity—in name they reverse, in reality they meet.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha is called True Correctness, the Way Correct Unity—in name reversed, in reality united.

sentences.zh: 在名則反，在實則合。

translations.literal: In name they reverse, in reality they meet.
translations.idiomatic: In name reversed, in reality united.

sentences.zh: 但無生之教賒，無死之化切，切法可以進謙弱，賒法可以退誇強。

translations.literal: Yet the teaching of no-birth is slow, the transformation of no-death is urgent; the urgent method can advance humility and weakness, the slow method can retire pride and strength.
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of no-birth is gradual, no-death urgent; urgency advances humility, gradualness retires pride.

sentences.zh: 佛教文而博，道教質而精，精非粗人所信，博非精人所能。

translations.literal: Buddhist teaching is literary and broad, Daoist teaching plain and refined; refinement is not believed by the coarse, breadth not mastered by the refined.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is literary and broad, Daoism plain and refined; the coarse cannot believe refinement, the refined cannot master breadth.

sentences.zh: 佛言華而引，道言實而抑，抑則明者獨進，引則昧者競前。

translations.literal: Buddhist words are florid and draw forward, Daoist words solid and restrain; restraint lets the clear advance alone, drawing lets the dim race ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha's words flower and draw the crowd forward; the Way's words are solid and hold back—the clear advance alone, the dim race ahead.

sentences.zh: 佛經繁而顯，道經簡而幽，幽則妙門難見，顯則正路易遵。

translations.literal: Buddhist scriptures are complex and manifest, Daoist scriptures simple and hidden; hidden makes the subtle gate hard to see, manifest makes the correct path easy to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist sutras are complex and plain to see; Daoist scriptures simple and hidden—hidden obscures the subtle gate, manifest eases the true path.

sentences.zh: 此二法之辨也。

translations.literal: This is the discrimination of the two teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the distinction between the two teachings.

sentences.zh: 聖匠無心，方圓有體，器既殊用，教亦易施。

translations.literal: The sage craftsman is without mind; square and round have their forms; vessels differ in use, teaching also changes in application.
translations.idiomatic: The sage craftsman has no fixed mind; square and round have form; vessels differ, and teaching changes with them.

sentences.zh: 佛是破惡之方，道是興善之術，興善則自然為高，破惡則勇猛為貴。

translations.literal: Buddha is the method of breaking evil, the Way the art of raising good; raising good, then naturally one is lofty; breaking evil, then courage is honored.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha breaks evil, the Way raises good; raising good lifts one naturally, breaking evil honors courage.

sentences.zh: 佛跡光大，宜以化物。

translations.literal: The Buddha's traces are broad and bright, fit to transform things.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha's traces are broad and bright, fit to transform the multitude.

sentences.zh: 道跡密微，利用為己。

translations.literal: The Way's traces are subtle and close, to be used for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The Way's traces are subtle and close, for one's own use.

sentences.zh: 優劣之分，大略在茲。

translations.literal: The division of superior and inferior lies roughly here.
translations.idiomatic: Superior and inferior divide roughly here.

sentences.zh: 夫蹲夷之儀，婁羅之辯，各出彼俗，自相聆解。

translations.literal: The ceremonies of crouching Yi and the dialectic of coarse robes each spring from those customs and are understood among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Squatting Yi rites and coarse-robe debate each spring from their own customs and are understood within them.

sentences.zh: 猶蟲躍鳥聒，何足述效。

translations.literal: Like insects leaping and birds crying—what worth is there in imitating them?
translations.idiomatic: Like insects leaping and birds crying—what is there to imitate?

sentences.zh: 歡雖同二法，而意黨道教。

translations.literal: Though Huan treated the two teachings as the same, in mind he favored the Daoist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Though Huan treated both teachings as one, in heart he favored Daoism.

sentences.zh: 宋司徒袁粲托為道人通公駁之。

translations.literal: Song's Minister of Works Yuan Can had the Daoist Tong Gong refute him on commission.
translations.idiomatic: Song Minister of Works Yuan Can had the Daoist Tong Gong answer him.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: In summary it says:
translations.idiomatic: In summary:

sentences.zh: 白日停光，恒星隱照，誕降之應，事在老先，似非入關，方昭斯瑞。

translations.literal: The white sun stops its light, the fixed stars hide their illumination; the response of descent into birth occurred in remote antiquity—it seems not to be on entering the Pass that this omen was revealed.
translations.idiomatic: The white sun halted, fixed stars hid their light—the sign of descent came in remote antiquity, not merely on Laozi's entering the Pass.

sentences.zh: 又西域之記，佛經之說，俗以膝行為禮，不慕蹲坐為恭。

translations.literal: Again, in western records and Buddhist scriptures, custom takes knee-walking as ritual and does not admire squat-sitting as respect.
translations.idiomatic: Western records and Buddhist scriptures take knee-walking as ritual, not squat-sitting as respect.

sentences.zh: 道以三遶為虔，不尚踞傲為肅。

translations.literal: The Way takes three circuits as devotion and does not honor sprawling pride as solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: The Way takes three circuits as devotion, not sprawling pride as solemnity.

sentences.zh: 豈專戎土，爰亦茲方。

translations.literal: How is it only the Rong land—here too it is thus.
translations.idiomatic: This is not only Rong custom—it exists here as well.

sentences.zh: 襄童謁帝，膝行而進，趙王見周，三環而止。

translations.literal: Xiang the lad visited the emperor, advancing on his knees; the King of Zhao received Zhou, halting after three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang the lad approached the emperor on his knees; the King of Zhao received Zhou and halted after three circuits.

sentences.zh: 今佛法垂化，或因或革。

translations.literal: Now the Buddhist teaching spreads transformation, sometimes following, sometimes changing.
translations.idiomatic: Now Buddhism spreads, sometimes following custom, sometimes changing it.

sentences.zh: 清信之士，容衣不改，息心之人，服貌必變。

translations.literal: Men of pure faith may keep their dress unchanged; men who quiet the heart must change their appearance.
translations.idiomatic: The devout may keep their dress; those who quiet the heart must change their appearance.

sentences.zh: 變本從道，不遵彼俗，俗風自殊，無患其亂。

translations.literal: Changing the root to follow the Way, not obeying their customs—customs differ by themselves, no fear of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: They change the root to follow the Way, not foreign custom—customs differ by nature, so no disorder follows.

sentences.zh: 孔、老、釋迦，其人或同，觀方設教，其道必異。

translations.literal: Confucius, Laozi, and Śākyamuni—their persons may be the same; viewing the region they set forth teaching, their Ways must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, Laozi, and Śākyamuni may be one in person; viewing the land they teach, their Ways must differ.

sentences.zh: 孔、老教俗為本，釋氏出世為宗，發軫既殊，其歸亦異。

translations.literal: Confucius and Laozi teach custom as root, the Śākya clan takes leaving the world as aim; their starting points already differ, their destinations also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius and Laozi root teaching in custom; Śākyamuni takes leaving the world as his aim—their starting points differ, and so do their destinations.

sentences.zh: 又仙化以變形為上，泥洹以陶神為先。

translations.literal: Again, immortal transformation takes changing form as highest, nirvana takes refining spirit as first.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal transformation prizes changing the body; nirvana prizes refining the spirit.

sentences.zh: 變形者白首還緇，而未能無死；

translations.literal: Changing form: white-haired return to black, yet unable to be without death;
translations.idiomatic: Changing form turns white hair black yet cannot escape death;

sentences.zh: 陶神者使塵惑日損，湛然常存。

translations.literal: refining spirit: making dust and delusion daily lessen, limpid and ever abiding.
translations.idiomatic: refining spirit lessens delusion day by day until clarity abides.

sentences.zh: 泥洹之道，無死之地，乖詭若此，何謂其同？

translations.literal: The way of nirvana is a land without death—if perverse and strange like this, what is called the same?
translations.idiomatic: Nirvana is a realm without death—if they diverge so wildly, how are they the same?

sentences.zh: 歡答曰：

translations.literal: Huan answered:
translations.idiomatic: Huan replied:

sentences.zh: 案道經之作，著自西周，佛經之來，始乎東漢。

translations.literal: Considering the composition of the Daoist classic, it was written in the Western Zhou; the coming of Buddhist scriptures began in the Eastern Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist classics were written in Western Zhou; Buddhist scriptures came in Eastern Han.

sentences.zh: 年踰八百，代懸數十。

translations.literal: Years exceed eight hundred, generations span dozens.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred years and dozens of reigns lie between them.

sentences.zh: 若謂黃、老雖久而濫在釋前，是呂尚盜陳恒之齊，劉季竊王莽之漢也。

translations.literal: If one says Huang-Lao, though long ago, wrongly precede the Buddha, it is Lü Shang stealing Chen Heng's Qi, Liu Ji stealing Wang Mang's Han.
translations.idiomatic: To say Huang-Lao wrongly precede Buddha is like Lü Shang stealing Chen Heng's Qi or Liu Bang stealing Wang Mang's Han.

sentences.zh: 又夷俗長跽，法與華異，翹左跂右，全是蹲踞。

translations.literal: Again, Yi custom favors long kneeling; ritual differs from Hua; raising the left and planting the right is entirely squatting.
translations.idiomatic: Yi custom favors long kneeling unlike Hua; raising the left foot while planting the right is pure squatting.

sentences.zh: 故周公禁之于前，仲尼誡之於後。

translations.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou forbade it before, Confucius warned of it after.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou forbade it early, Confucius warned of it later.

sentences.zh: 又佛起於戎，豈非戎俗素惡邪？

translations.literal: Again, Buddha arose among the Rong—are not the Rong by nature evil?
translations.idiomatic: Buddha arose among the Rong—are the Rong not evil by nature?

sentences.zh: 道出於華，豈非華風本善邪？

translations.literal: The Way arose among the Hua—are not the Hua by nature good?
translations.idiomatic: The Way arose among the Hua—are the Hua not good by nature?

sentences.zh: 今華風既變，惡同戎狄，佛來破之，良有以矣。

translations.literal: Now Hua custom has changed, evil like the Rong; Buddha came to break it—indeed there is reason.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hua custom has turned as vicious as the Rong; Buddha came to break it—and rightly so.

sentences.zh: 佛道實貴，故戒業可遵；

translations.literal: The Buddhist Way is truly honored, therefore its precepts may be followed;
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist Way is truly noble, so its precepts may be followed;

sentences.zh: 戎俗實賤，故言貌可棄。

translations.literal: Rong custom is truly base, therefore words and appearance may be cast off.
translations.idiomatic: Rong custom is truly base, so its manners may be cast off.

sentences.zh: 今諸華士女，氏族弗革，而露首偏踞，濫用夷禮。

translations.literal: Now Hua gentlemen and ladies, clans unchanged, yet bare-headed and squatting one-sidedly, recklessly use Yi ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hua men and women keep their clans yet go bare-headed and squatting, recklessly using Yi rites.

sentences.zh: 又若觀風流教，其道必異。

translations.literal: Again, if one views the wind and transforms teaching, the Way must differ.
translations.idiomatic: View the wind of each land and its teaching must differ.

sentences.zh: 佛非東華之道，道非西夷之法，魚鳥異川，永不相關。

translations.literal: Buddha is not the Way of eastern Hua, the Way is not the method of western Yi—fish and birds differ in their streams and never relate.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha is not eastern Hua's Way, the Way is not western Yi's method—fish and birds differ in stream and never meet.

sentences.zh: 安得老、釋二教，交行八表。

translations.literal: How could Laozi and Śākyamuni's two teachings cross the eight directions together?
translations.idiomatic: How could Laozi and Śākyamuni's teachings cross the realm together?

sentences.zh: 今佛既東流，道亦西邁，故知俗有精粗，教有文質。

translations.literal: Now Buddha has flowed east, the Way also marched west—thus one knows customs have coarse and fine, teachings literary and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha has flowed east, the Way marched west—custom has coarse and fine, teaching literary and plain.

sentences.zh: 然則道教執本以領末，佛教救末以存本。

translations.literal: Then the Daoist teaching holds the root to lead the branches, Buddhism saves the branches to preserve the root.
translations.idiomatic: Daoism holds the root to lead branches; Buddhism saves branches to preserve the root.

sentences.zh: 請問所歸，異在何許？

translations.literal: I ask where they return—where does the difference lie?
translations.idiomatic: I ask where they return—where does difference lie?

sentences.zh: 若以翦落為異，則胥靡翦落矣；

translations.literal: If one takes shorn hair as the difference, then convicts are shorn;
translations.idiomatic: If shorn hair is the difference, convicts are shorn;

sentences.zh: 若以立像為異，則俗巫立像矣。

translations.literal: if one takes setting up images as the difference, then vulgar shamans set up images.
translations.idiomatic: if setting up images is the difference, vulgar shamans set up images.

sentences.zh: 此非所歸，歸在常住，常住之象，常道孰異。

translations.literal: This is not where they return; return lies in the eternal abiding—the image of eternal abiding, how does the eternal Way differ?
translations.idiomatic: That is not the return; return lies in eternal abiding—and in eternal abiding, how does the eternal Way differ?

sentences.zh: 神仙有死，權便之說。

translations.literal: Immortals have death—a provisional doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Immortals die—that is a provisional teaching.

sentences.zh: 神仙是大化之總稱，非窮妙之至名。

translations.literal: Immortal is the general name of great transformation, not the utmost name of the wondrous extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal is the general name of great transformation, not the utmost of wonder.

sentences.zh: 至名無名，其有名者二十七品。

translations.literal: The utmost name is nameless; what has names are twenty-seven ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The utmost name is nameless; what has names are twenty-seven ranks.

sentences.zh: 仙變成真，真變成神，或謂之聖，各有九品。

translations.literal: Immortal transforms to true, true transforms to spirit, or is called sage—each has nine ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal becomes true, true becomes spirit, or is called sage—each has nine ranks.

sentences.zh: 品極則入空寂，無為無名。

translations.literal: When ranks reach the extreme one enters empty stillness, non-action and namelessness.
translations.idiomatic: At the rank's extreme one enters empty stillness, non-action, namelessness.

sentences.zh: 若服食茹芝，延壽萬億，壽盡則死，藥極則枯，此修考之士，非神仙之流也。

translations.literal: If eating elixirs and lichen to prolong life a hundred million years—when life ends one dies, when medicine is exhausted one withers—these are cultivators of longevity, not of the immortal stream.
