translations.idiomatic: Those who eat elixirs and lichen to live a hundred million years still die when life ends and wither when medicine fails—they cultivate longevity, not immortality.

sentences.zh: 明僧紹正二教論，以為「佛明其宗，老全其生。

translations.literal: Ming Sengshao's Correcting the Two Teachings holds that "Buddha clarifies its aim, Laozi completes life.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Sengshao's Correcting the Two Teachings says, "Buddha clarifies its aim, Laozi completes life.

sentences.zh: 守生者蔽，明宗者通。

translations.literal: Guarding life is obscured, clarifying aim is penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Guarding life blinds; clarifying aim opens.

sentences.zh: 今道家稱長生不死，名補天曹，大乖老、莊立言本理」。

translations.literal: Now Daoists claim long life without death, naming it filling the celestial register—greatly at odds with Laozi and Zhuangzi's founding reason."
translations.idiomatic: Daoists now claim eternal life and filling the celestial register—far from Laozi and Zhuangzi's founding intent."

sentences.zh: 文惠太子、竟陵王子良並好釋法，吳興孟景翼為道士，太子召入玄圃，眾僧大會。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince of Jingling Zi Liang both loved Buddhist law; Meng Jingyi of Wu was a Daoist; the crown prince summoned him into the Dark Garden for a great assembly of monks.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Jingling Zi Liang loved Buddhism; Wu's Meng Jingyi was a Daoist. The crown prince summoned him to the Dark Garden for a great assembly of monks.

sentences.zh: 子良使景翼禮佛，景翼不肯。

translations.literal: Zi Liang had Jingyi bow to the Buddha; Jingyi refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Liang ordered Jingyi to bow to Buddha; Jingyi refused.

sentences.zh: 子良送十地經與之，景翼造正一論，大略曰：「寶積雲，'佛以一音廣說法'。

translations.literal: Zi Liang sent him the Ten Grounds Sutra; Jingyi composed the Treatise on Correct Unity, in summary saying: "In the Treasure Accumulation it says, 'The Buddha with one sound broadly expounds the Law.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Liang sent him the Ten Grounds Sutra; Jingyi wrote the Treatise on Correct Unity: "In Treasure Accumulation, 'The Buddha with one sound broadly expounds the Law.

sentences.zh: 老子雲，'聖人抱一以為天下式'。

translations.literal: Laozi says, 'The sage embraces unity as the world's pattern.'
translations.idiomatic: Laozi says, 'The sage embraces unity as the world's pattern.'

sentences.zh: 一之為妙，空玄絕於有境，神化贍於無窮。

translations.literal: The wonder of unity: empty mystery beyond the realm of being, spirit transformation sufficient in the endless.
translations.idiomatic: Unity's wonder: empty mystery beyond being, spirit transformation endless.

sentences.zh: 為萬物而無為，處一數而無數。

translations.literal: Acting for the myriad things yet non-acting, dwelling in one number yet numberless.
translations.idiomatic: Acting for all things yet non-acting, dwelling in one yet beyond number.

sentences.zh: 莫之能名，強號為一。

translations.literal: None can name it, forcibly called unity.
translations.idiomatic: None can name it—forced, it is called unity.

sentences.zh: 在佛曰'實相'，在道曰'玄牝 '。

translations.literal: In Buddhism called 'true mark,' in the Way called 'mysterious female.'
translations.idiomatic: In Buddhism 'true mark,' in the Way 'mysterious female.'

sentences.zh: 道之大象，即佛之法身。

translations.literal: The great image of the Way is the dharma-body of Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: The Way's great image is Buddha's dharma-body.

sentences.zh: 以不守之守守法身，以不執之執執大象。

translations.literal: With non-holding holding the dharma-body, with non-grasping grasping the great image.
translations.idiomatic: Not holding, hold the dharma-body; not grasping, grasp the great image.

sentences.zh: 但物有八萬四千行，說有八萬四千法。

translations.literal: Yet things have eighty-four thousand practices, exposition has eighty-four thousand methods.
translations.idiomatic: Things have eighty-four thousand practices, teaching eighty-four thousand methods.

sentences.zh: 法乃至於無數，行亦達於無央，等級隨緣，須導歸一。

translations.literal: Methods reach even to numberlessness, practices also reach the boundless; ranks follow conditions, all must be guided back to unity.
translations.idiomatic: Methods reach beyond number, practices to the boundless; ranks follow conditions, all guided back to unity.

sentences.zh: 歸一曰回向，向正即無邪。

translations.literal: Returning to unity is called turning toward; turning toward correctness then has no perversity.
translations.idiomatic: Return to unity is turning toward; turning toward correctness leaves no perversity.

sentences.zh: 邪觀既遣，億善日新。

translations.literal: Perverse views dispelled, billions of goods renewed daily.
translations.idiomatic: Perverse views gone, goodness renews daily by the billion.

sentences.zh: 三五四六，隨用而施，獨立不改，絕學無憂。

translations.literal: Three, five, four, six—applied as needed; standing alone unchanging, cutting off learning without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Three, five, four, six—applied as needed; standing alone unchanged, cutting off learning without worry.

sentences.zh: 曠劫諸聖，共遵斯一。

translations.literal: Through kalpas the sages together honor this unity.
translations.idiomatic: Through kalpas all sages honor this one unity.

sentences.zh: 老、釋未始於嘗分，迷者分之而未合。

translations.literal: Laozi and Śākyamuni never began by dividing; the lost divide what was never separate.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi and Śākyamuni never divided; the lost split what was never apart.

sentences.zh: 億善遍修，修遍成聖，雖十號千稱，終不能盡。

translations.literal: Billions of goods broadly cultivated, cultivation broad becoming sage—though ten titles and a thousand names, in the end they cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivate goodness without end until sagehood—ten titles, a thousand names, yet never exhausted.

sentences.zh: 終不能盡，豈可思議。」

translations.literal: In the end they cannot be exhausted—how could it not be beyond thought?"
translations.idiomatic: Never exhausted—how could it not be beyond thought?"

sentences.zh: 司徒從事中郎張融作門律云：「道之與佛，逗極無二。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Zhang Rong of the Ministry of Works composed a gate-rule saying: "The Way and Buddha, their ultimate convergence has no two.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong, Attendant of the Ministry of Works, wrote a gate-rule: "Way and Buddha converge without two.

sentences.zh: 吾見道士與道人戰儒墨，道人與道士辨是非。

translations.literal: I see Daoists and Buddhist masters fighting Confucians and Mohists, Buddhist masters and Daoists disputing right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I see Daoists fight Confucians, Buddhist masters dispute Daoists.

sentences.zh: 昔有鴻飛天首，積遠難亮，越人以為鳧，楚人以為乙。

translations.literal: Of old a swan flew at heaven's head, accumulated distance hard to see; Yue men thought it a duck, Chu men thought it the graph yi.
translations.idiomatic: Once a swan flew high beyond sight; Yue men called it a duck, Chu men a mere hook-shaped stroke.

sentences.zh: 人自楚、越，鴻常一耳。」

translations.literal: Men themselves were Chu and Yue, the swan was always one."
translations.idiomatic: Men were Chu and Yue; the swan was always one."

sentences.zh: 以示太子僕周顒。

translations.literal: He showed it to Palace Attendant Zhou Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He showed this to Palace Attendant Zhou Yong.

sentences.zh: 顒難之曰：「虛無法性，其寂雖同，位寂之方，其旨則別。

translations.literal: Yong disputed it, saying: "Empty non-being and dharma-nature, their stillness though the same, the place of stillness, their aim then differs.
translations.idiomatic: Yong objected: "Emptiness and dharma-nature share stillness, yet the locus of stillness differs.

sentences.zh: 論所謂'逗極無二'者，為逗極於虛無，當無二於法性邪。

translations.literal: What your treatise calls 'ultimate convergence has no two'—is convergence ultimate in emptiness, that there should be no two in dharma-nature?
translations.idiomatic: You say 'convergence has no two'—is convergence ultimate in emptiness, so dharma-nature has no two?

sentences.zh: 足下所宗之本一物為鴻乙耳，驅馳佛道，無免二末，未知高鑒，緣何識本？

translations.literal: The root you honor is one thing as swan and yi; driving Buddhist and Daoist ways, you cannot escape two ends—unknown is your lofty mirror, on what do you recognize the root?
translations.idiomatic: You take one thing as swan and yi, yet drive Buddhist and Daoist ways—you cannot escape two ends. On what mirror do you know the root?

sentences.zh: 輕而宗之，其有旨乎。」

translations.literal: Light yet honoring it—is there meaning?"
translations.idiomatic: You treat it lightly yet honor it—is there sense in that?"

sentences.zh: 往復文多不載。

translations.literal: The exchanged writings are many and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Their exchanged writings were many and are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 歡口不辯，善於著論。

translations.literal: Huan was not skilled in debate but good at composing treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was no debater but excelled at treatises.

sentences.zh: 又注王弼易二系，學者傳之。

translations.literal: He also annotated Wang Bi's two commentaries on the Changes, which scholars transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated Wang Bi's commentaries on the Changes, which scholars passed on.

sentences.zh: 知將終，賦詩言志曰：「五塗無恒宅，三清有常舍。

translations.literal: Knowing he would end, he composed a poem stating his will: "The five paths have no constant dwelling, the three clarities have a constant abode.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing his end, he wrote a poem: "The five paths have no fixed home, the three clarities a constant dwelling.

sentences.zh: 精氣因天行，遊魂隨物化。

translations.literal: Essence and breath follow heaven's movement, the roaming soul follows things in transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Essence and breath follow heaven; the roaming soul follows things in change.

sentences.zh: 鵬從適大海，蜩鳩之桑柘。

translations.literal: The peng goes to the great sea, the cicada and dove to mulberry and catalpa.
translations.idiomatic: The peng reaches the great sea, cicada and dove the mulberry.

sentences.zh: 達生任去留，善死均日夜。

translations.literal: Attaining life, accept going or staying; a good death equals day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In life accept going or staying; in good death, day equals night.

sentences.zh: 委命安所乘，何方不可駕。

translations.literal: Entrust life to what you ride—what direction cannot be driven?
translations.idiomatic: Entrust life to what you ride—what road cannot be taken?

sentences.zh: 翹心企前覺，融然從此謝。」

translations.literal: Raise the heart to look to former awakening, melt away and from here depart."
translations.idiomatic: Lift the heart toward prior awakening, melt away and depart."

sentences.zh: 自克死日，自擇葬時，卒於剡山，時年六十四。

translations.literal: From the day he fixed his death he chose his burial time himself, and died on Mount Shan at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he chose his death he fixed his burial; he died on Mount Shan at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 身體香軟，道家謂之屍解仙化焉。

translations.literal: His body was fragrant and soft; Daoists called this corpse-dissolution and immortal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: His body was fragrant and soft; Daoists called it corpse-dissolution and ascension.

sentences.zh: 還葬舊墓，木連理生墓側。

translations.literal: He was buried at his old tomb; trees joined in one trunk beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in his old tomb; trees joined trunk beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 縣令江山圖表狀，武帝詔歡諸子撰歡文議三十卷。

translations.literal: The magistrate Jiang Shantu memorialized; Emperor Wu ordered Huan's sons to compile thirty scrolls of Huan's writings and discussions.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Jiang Shantu memorialized; Emperor Wu ordered Huan's sons to compile thirty scrolls of his writings.

sentences.zh: 又始興人廬度字孝章，亦有道術。

translations.literal: Also Lu Du of Shixing, styled Xiaozhang, also had Daoist arts.
translations.idiomatic: Also Lu Du of Shixing, styled Xiaozhang, possessed Daoist arts.

sentences.zh: 少隨張永北侵魏。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Zhang Yong north to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he followed Zhang Yong north against Wei.

sentences.zh: 永敗，魏人追急，阻淮水不得過。

translations.literal: Yong was defeated; Wei men pursued hotly; blocked by the Huai River they could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was defeated; Wei pursuers pressed hard; the Huai blocked their crossing.

sentences.zh: 度心誓曰：「若得免死，從今不復殺生。」

translations.literal: Du vowed in his heart: "If I escape death, from now I will no longer kill living things."
translations.idiomatic: Du vowed: "If I escape death, I will never kill again."

sentences.zh: 須臾見兩楯流來，接之得過。

translations.literal: In a moment he saw two shields floating by; taking them he got across.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two shields floated by; he used them to cross.

sentences.zh: 後隱居廬陵西昌三顧山，鳥獸隨之。

translations.literal: Later he lived in seclusion on Mount Sangu of Xichang in Luling; birds and beasts followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lived on Mount Sangu in Xichang, Luling; birds and beasts followed him.

sentences.zh: 夜有鹿觸其壁，度曰：「汝勿壞我壁。」

translations.literal: At night a deer bumped his wall; Du said: "Do not break my wall."
translations.idiomatic: At night a deer bumped his wall; Du said, "Do not break my wall."

sentences.zh: 鹿應聲去。

translations.literal: The deer answered and left.
translations.idiomatic: The deer left at once.

sentences.zh: 屋前有池養魚，皆名呼之，次第來取食乃去。

translations.literal: Before his house was a pool where he kept fish; he called each by name; they came in order to take food and then left.
translations.idiomatic: He kept fish in a pool before his house, called each by name; they came in order, ate, and left.

sentences.zh: 逆知死年月，與親友別。

translations.literal: He foreknew the year and month of his death and took leave of kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He foreknew his death, bade kin and friends farewell.

sentences.zh: 永明末，以壽終。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming he died of age.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming he died at his full span.

sentences.zh: 杜京產

translations.literal: Du Jingchan
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingchan

sentences.zh: 杜京產，字景齊，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Du Jingchan, styled Jingqi, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingchan, styled Jingqi, was from Qiantang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖運，劉毅衛軍參軍。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yun was a staff officer in Liu Yi's Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun was staff officer in Liu Yi's Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 父道鞠，州從事，善彈棋。

translations.literal: Father Daoju was a commandery aide and skilled at pitch-pot.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoju was a commandery aide, skilled at pitch-pot.

sentences.zh: 京產少恬靜，閉意榮宦，頗涉文義，專修黃、老。

translations.literal: Jingchan from youth was tranquil, closed his mind to glory and office, dipped somewhat into literary meaning, and devoted himself solely to Huang-Lao.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jingchan was tranquil, shunning glory and office; he read widely and devoted himself to Huang-Lao.

sentences.zh: 會稽孔覬，清剛有峻節，一見而為款交。

translations.literal: Kong Gui of Kuaiji was pure, firm, and had stern integrity; on one meeting he became a warm friend.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui of Kuaiji was pure and stern; at one meeting they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 郡命主簿，州辟從事，稱疾去。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him chief clerk, the province summoned him as aide; he pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery made him chief clerk, the province summoned him as aide; he pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 與同郡顧歡同契。

translations.literal: He was of one bond with Gu Huan of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He and Gu Huan of the same commandery were sworn friends.

sentences.zh: 于始寧東山開舍授學。

translations.literal: At East Mountain in Shining he opened a lodge and taught.
translations.idiomatic: On East Mountain in Shining he opened a school.

sentences.zh: 齊建元中，武陵王曄為會稽，齊高帝遣儒士劉瓛入東為曄講，瓛故往與之遊，曰：「杜生，當今之台、尚也。」

translations.literal: In the Jianyuan era of Qi, Prince Ye of Wuling was governor of Kuaiji; Emperor Gao of Qi sent the Confucian Liu Huan east to lecture for Ye; Huan therefore went to associate with him, saying: "Master Du is today's Tai and Shang."
translations.idiomatic: In Qi's Jianyuan era Prince Ye of Wuling governed Kuaiji; Emperor Gao sent Liu Huan east to lecture for the prince. Huan visited Jingchan and said, "Master Du is today's Tai and Shang."

sentences.zh: 京產請瓛至山舍講書，傾資供待。

translations.literal: Jingchan invited Huan to his mountain lodge to lecture, spending his whole substance to host him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchan invited Huan to lecture at his mountain lodge and spent all he had to host him.

sentences.zh: 子棲躬自屣履，為瓛生徒下食。

translations.literal: His son Qi personally put on sandals and served food for Huan's students.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi wore sandals himself and served Huan's students their meals.

sentences.zh: 孔珪、周顒、謝瀹並致書以通殷勤。

translations.literal: Kong Gui, Zhou Yong, and Xie Tiao all sent letters to express warm regard.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui, Zhou Yong, and Xie Tiao all wrote letters of warm regard.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，珪及光祿大夫陸澄、祠部尚書虞悰、太子右率沈約、司徒右長史張融表薦京產，徵為奉朝請，不至。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming, Gui and Grand Master of Splendid Honors Lu Cheng, Minister of Rites Yu Kai, Right Leader of the Heir Apparent Shen Yue, and Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry Zhang Rong jointly memorialized recommending Jingchan; he was summoned as Court Gentleman for the Assembly but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming's tenth year Gui, Lu Cheng, Yu Kai, Shen Yue, and Zhang Rong jointly recommended Jingchan; he was summoned as Court Gentleman for the Assembly but did not come.

sentences.zh: 於會稽日門山聚徒教授。

translations.literal: At Rimen Mountain in Kuaiji he gathered disciples and taught.
translations.idiomatic: At Rimen Mountain in Kuaiji he gathered disciples and taught.

sentences.zh: 建武初，征員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was summoned as Outer Gentleman Attendant at Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu he was summoned as Outer Gentleman Attendant at Leisure.

sentences.zh: 京產曰：「莊生持釣，豈為白璧所回。」

translations.literal: Jingchan said: "Zhuangzi holding his line—would he be turned by a white jade?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingchan said, "Zhuangzi held his line—would a white jade turn him?"

sentences.zh: 辭疾不就，卒。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and did not go, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness, did not go, and died.

sentences.zh: 會稽山陰人孔道徽，守志業不仕，與京產友善。

translations.literal: Kong Daohui of Shanyin in Kuaiji kept his resolve and would not serve; he was friendly with Jingchan.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daohui of Shanyin in Kuaiji kept his resolve and would not serve; he was Jingchan's friend.

sentences.zh: 道徽父佑至行通神，隱於四明山，嘗見山谷中有數百斛錢，視之如瓦石不異。

translations.literal: Daohui's father You had utmost conduct penetrating the spirit, hiding on Mount Siming; he once saw in a valley several hundred piculs of cash, which to his eyes were like tiles and stones no different.
translations.idiomatic: Daohui's father You had conduct that touched the spirits and hid on Mount Siming; once he saw hundreds of piculs of cash in a valley and took it for tile and stone.

sentences.zh: 采樵者競取，入手即成沙礫。

translations.literal: Woodcutters who snatched it found it turn to gravel in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Woodcutters who seized it found it turn to gravel in their hands.

sentences.zh: 曾有鹿中箭來投佑，佑為之養創，愈然後去。

translations.literal: Once a deer wounded by an arrow came to throw itself on You; You nursed its wound until healed, then it left.
translations.idiomatic: Once a wounded deer came to You; he nursed it until healed, then it left.

sentences.zh: 太守王僧虔與張緒書曰：「孔佑，敬康曾孫也。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Sengqian wrote to Zhang Xu: "Kong You is a great-grandson of Jingkang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Sengqian wrote Zhang Xu: "Kong You is Jingkang's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 行動幽祗，德標松桂，引為主簿，遂不可屈。

translations.literal: His conduct moves the hidden powers, his virtue marks pine and cassia; I recommended him as chief clerk, yet he could not be bent.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct moves the hidden powers, his virtue like pine and cassia; I made him chief clerk, yet he would not bend.

sentences.zh: 此古之遺德也。」

translations.literal: This is the remnant virtue of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: This is virtue remnant from antiquity."

sentences.zh: 道徽少厲高行，能世其家風。

translations.literal: Daohui from youth cultivated lofty conduct and could inherit his family's wind.
translations.idiomatic: Daohui from youth cultivated lofty conduct and inherited his family's way.

sentences.zh: 隱居南山，終身不窺都邑。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion on South Mountain, all his life not peeping at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on South Mountain and never looked toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷為揚州，辟西曹書佐，不至。

translations.literal: Prince Ye of Yuzhang was governor of Yang Province and summoned him as Western Cao Secretary; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ye of Yuzhang, governor of Yang, summoned him as Western Cao Secretary; he did not come.

sentences.zh: 鄉里宗慕之。

translations.literal: The village and clan admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Village and clan admired him.

sentences.zh: 道徽兄子總，有操行，遇饑寒不可得衣食，縣令吳興丘仲孚薦之，除竟陵王侍郎，竟不至。

translations.literal: Daohui's elder brother's son Zong had moral conduct; encountering hunger and cold he could not obtain food or clothing; Magistrate Qiu Zhongfu of Wuxing recommended him, appointing him Attendant to the Prince of Jingling, yet he never came.
translations.idiomatic: Daohui's nephew Zong had moral conduct but in hunger and cold lacked food and clothing; Magistrate Qiu Zhongfu recommended him as Attendant to the Prince of Jingling, yet he never came.

sentences.zh: 永明中，會稽鍾山有人姓蔡，不知名，隱山中，養鼠數千頭，呼來即來，遣去即去。

translations.literal: In Yongming, on Mount Zhong in Kuaiji there was a man surnamed Cai whose name is unknown, hiding in the mountains, raising several thousand rats; calling them they came, sending them they went.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming on Mount Zhong in Kuaiji a man surnamed Cai, name unknown, lived in the hills raising thousands of rats—they came when called and went when sent.

sentences.zh: 言語狂易，時謂之謫仙，不知所終。

translations.literal: His speech was wild and easy; men of the time called him a banished immortal; no one knows his end.
translations.idiomatic: His speech was wild; men called him a banished immortal; none knows his end.

sentences.zh: 京產高祖子恭以來及子棲世傳五斗米道不替。

translations.literal: Since Jingchan's high ancestor Zigong, the five-peck-rice Way has been transmitted through the generations to his son Qi without lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jingchan's ancestor Zigong, the Five Pecks of Rice teaching passed through Qi without lapse.

sentences.zh: 棲字孟山，善清言，能彈琴。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Mengshan, was skilled in pure talk and could play the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, styled Mengshan, excelled at pure talk and played the zither.

sentences.zh: 刺史齊豫章王嶷聞其名，辟議曹從事，仍轉西曹書佐。

translations.literal: Governor Prince Ye of Yuzhang heard his name and summoned him as Aide for Discussion; he was transferred to Western Cao Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ye of Yuzhang heard his name and summoned him as Aide for Discussion, then Western Cao Secretary.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良數致禮接。

translations.literal: Prince Zi Liang of Jingling repeatedly sent courteous invitations.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingling Zi Liang repeatedly invited him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒何胤掌禮，又重棲，以為學士，掌昏冠儀。

translations.literal: Director of Studies He Yin presided over ritual and again valued Qi, making him Academician in charge of marriage and cap ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Studies He Yin valued Qi, made him Academician in charge of marriage and cap rites.

sentences.zh: 以父老歸養。

translations.literal: Because his father was old he returned to nourish him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father aged he returned home to care for him.

sentences.zh: 棲肥白長壯，及京產病，旬日間便皮骨自支。

translations.literal: Qi was fat, white, tall, and strong; when Jingchan fell ill, within ten days or so he was skin and bone supporting himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had been fat, fair, tall, and strong; when Jingchan fell ill, within ten days he was skin on bone.

sentences.zh: 京產亡，水漿不入口七日，晨夜不罷哭，不食鹽菜。

translations.literal: When Jingchan died, Qi took no water or broth for seven days, weeping morning and night without cease, eating no salt or vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingchan died, Qi took no food or drink for seven days, wept without cease, ate no salt or vegetables.

sentences.zh: 每營買祭奠，身自看視，號泣不自持。

translations.literal: Each time he arranged offerings he personally oversaw them, wailing beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: Each offering he oversaw himself, wailing beyond control.

sentences.zh: 朔望節歲，絕而復續，嘔血數升。

translations.literal: On the new and full moon and festival days he would break off and resume, vomiting blood by the sheng.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moons and festivals he would break off and resume, vomiting blood by the pint.

sentences.zh: 時何胤、謝朏並隱東山，遺書敦譬，誡以毀滅。

translations.literal: At the time He Yin and Xie Tiao both lived in seclusion on East Mountain; they sent letters earnestly admonishing him, warning against self-destruction.
translations.idiomatic: He Yin and Xie Tiao, both reclusive on East Mountain, wrote urging him not to destroy himself.

sentences.zh: 至祥禫，暮夢見其父，慟哭而絕。

translations.literal: At the end of the mourning rites, one evening he dreamed he saw his father, wailed in grief, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, one evening he dreamed of his father, wailed, and died.

sentences.zh: 初，胤兄點見棲歎曰：「卿風韻如此，雖獲嘉譽，不永年矣。」

translations.literal: At first Yin's elder brother Dian, on seeing Qi, sighed: "With such bearing as yours, though you win fine praise, you will not live long."
translations.idiomatic: Once Yin's brother Dian, seeing Qi, sighed: "With such bearing you will win praise but not long life."

sentences.zh: 卒時年三十六，當時咸嗟惜焉。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-six; all at the time sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six; all mourned him.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，剡縣有小兒年八歲，與母俱得赤班病，母死，家人以小兒猶惡，不令其知。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, in Shan County there was a small boy eight years old who with his mother both contracted red macules; the mother died; the family, because the boy was still ill, did not let him know.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu's second year in Shan County an eight-year-old boy and his mother both caught red macules; the mother died; the family, thinking the boy still ill, hid it from him.

sentences.zh: 小兒疑之，問云：「母嘗數問我病，昨來覺聲羸，今不復問，何也？」

translations.literal: The boy suspected and asked: "Mother often asked after my illness; yesterday I felt her voice weak, today she no longer asks—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The boy grew suspicious: "Mother always asked after my illness; yesterday her voice was weak, today she does not ask—why?"

sentences.zh: 因自投下床，扶匐至母屍側，頓絕而死。

translations.literal: He then threw himself from the bed, crawled to his mother's corpse, and died in a fit.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself from the bed, crawled to his mother's corpse, and died in a fit.

sentences.zh: 鄉鄰告之縣令宗善才，求表廬，事竟不行。

translations.literal: The village reported to Magistrate Zong Shancai, who sought to memorialize a commemorative lodge; in the end it was not done.
translations.idiomatic: The village reported to Magistrate Zong Shancai, who sought to memorialize a commemorative lodge; in the end it was not granted.
